definition_zh: 爵士乐；爵士舞；爵士风格；（口语）活力、花样
definition_en: a style of music with strong rhythm and free improvisation, developed by African American musicians
core_image: 小号手闭着眼，音符从乐器里甩出去，鼓手在旁跟着改动节奏
scene: 午夜的小酒吧里，几个人轮流即兴，观众用脚打拍子。 The band played jazz until two in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 jazz 是「爵士乐」（第 1 个义项：以强烈节奏与即兴为特点的音乐），句意为乐队一直演奏爵士乐到凌晨两点。画面里的物件：酒吧、小号、鼓、打拍的脚。

pos.zh: 动词：（口语）使其更热闹；即兴演奏

derivatives.zh: 由 jazz 加 -y 构成，义为「爵士风格的；花哨的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「兴奋的」
由 jazz 与 man 复合，义为「爵士乐手」

senses.title: The music itself
senses.definition: a style of music with strong rhythm, swing, and a large share of improvisation
senses.definitionCN: 节奏强烈、摇摆感明显、即兴成分很大的音乐风格
senses.example: Jazz was born in the southern United States.
senses.exampleCN: 爵士乐诞生于美国南部。
senses.why: The musical sense is the core of the word and the source of every other meaning.
senses.whyCN: 音乐义是这个词的核心，也是其他意义之源。

senses.title: The style attached to it
senses.definition: the manner, dress, or way of playing that belongs to jazz performance
senses.definitionCN: 属于爵士演奏的方式、穿着或风格
senses.example: The cafe has a jazz feel with dark wood and warm lights.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆用深色木头和暖灯营造出爵士味。
senses.why: A style can be named by the music it evokes, even when no music is playing.
senses.whyCN: 即使不放音乐，一种风格也可以借它唤起的音乐来命名。

senses.title: A dance to that music
senses.definition: a lively dance performed to jazz music, later a stage dance form
senses.definitionCN: 随爵士乐跳的活泼舞蹈，后来发展成舞台舞种
senses.example: Students learn jazz in the dance class.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在舞蹈课上学习爵士舞。
senses.why: Dancing grew with the music, and the name travelled with the rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈随音乐一同成长，名字也随着节奏一起走。

senses.title: Liveliness or energy
senses.definition: an informal use for energy, excitement, or a lively quality in something
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指活力、兴奋或某种生动特质
senses.example: The new colours gave the room some jazz.
senses.exampleCN: 新的色彩给房间添了些活力。
senses.why: Jazz as lively music becomes a word for liveliness itself.
senses.whyCN: 爵士乐这种活泼的音乐，本身就成了「活泼」的代称。

senses.title: To make lively
senses.definition: to add decoration or energy to something so that it becomes more interesting
senses.definitionCN: 给某物增添装饰或活力，使其更有趣
senses.example: They jazzed up the menu for the holiday season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为节日季把菜单做得更花哨。
senses.why: The verb takes the lively quality of the noun and hands it to another thing.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词里那股活泼劲儿交到别的东西身上。

intro.en: Jazz appeared in print around 1912 for baseball slang and by the late 1910s for music; its deeper origin is still disputed.
intro.cn: jazz 约在 1912 年出现在报纸上是棒球俚语，到 1910 年代末指音乐，更深层的来源至今仍有争议。

items.en: Early records of jazz describe energy and liveliness, not yet music.
items.cn: 早期记录里的 jazz 指精力旺盛、活泼，还不是音乐。

items.en: The word spread from California newspapers in the late 1910s.
items.cn: 这个词在 1910 年代末从加州报纸传开。

items.en: New Orleans bands took jazz as the name of their music around 1917.
items.cn: 新奥尔良的乐队约在 1917 年用 jazz 称呼他们的音乐。

items.en: The music came from African American communities, including brass bands and blues.
items.cn: 这种音乐来自非裔美国人社群，包括铜管乐队与蓝调。

items.en: Jazz became a word for its style and later for liveliness in general.
items.cn: jazz 先成为风格之名，后来又泛指活泼。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jazz- family; the near-meaning group holds music styles and related performance words.
note.cn: 形近组是 jazz- 词族；近义组收音乐风格与演出相关词。

entries.definition: In the style of jazz, or bright and showy.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「爵士风的；花哨的」。

entries.definition: A musician who plays jazz.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「爵士乐手」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Very excited.
entries.definitionCN: 口语形容词，义为「兴奋的」。

entries.definition: A slow sad music form from African American tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「蓝调」，节奏更慢、情绪更沉。

entries.definition: A strong rhythmic style related to jazz.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「摇摆乐」，是爵士的近亲风格。

entries.definition: To make up music as you play it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「即兴演奏」，是爵士的核心手法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the slang sense of energy to the New Orleans bands.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从俚语里的「活力」走到新奥尔良的乐队。

normal.en: Jazz began as US slang for liveliness.
normal.cn: jazz 起初是美国俚语，指活力。

normal.en: New Orleans bands named the music jazz around 1917.
normal.cn: 新奥尔良乐队约在 1917 年把这种音乐叫作 jazz。

normal.en: Jazzy means in the style of jazz, or showy.
normal.cn: jazzy 意为爵士风的，或花哨的。

normal.en: Jazz up means to give something more life.
normal.cn: jazz up 意为给某物添生气。

normal.en: The deeper origin of jazz is still unknown.
normal.cn: jazz 更深层的来源至今不明。

abstract.en: Jazz is music that changes while you listen.
abstract.cn: 爵士是你听着它就在变的音乐。

abstract.en: A horn throws a line, and the drums answer back.
abstract.cn: 号甩出一句，鼓接回一句。

abstract.en: Liveliness itself can be called jazz.
abstract.cn: 活泼劲儿本身也可以被叫作 jazz。

examples.en: She listens to jazz while she works.
examples.cn: 她工作时听爵士乐。

examples.en: The festival mixes jazz with local folk songs.
examples.cn: 这个音乐节把爵士乐与当地民歌混在一起。

examples.en: They jazzed up the old hall with bright lights.
examples.cn: 他们用明快的灯光让旧礼堂热闹起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎兹」—— 音一扎一响，就是即兴摇摆的味儿

root: 美国俚语 jazz（约 1912 年出现，初指活力）→ 1910 年代末从西海岸报纸传开 → 1917 年前后新奥尔良乐队用于音乐 → 二十世纪扩展为风格与「活力」义。同族有 jazzy、jazzman。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the music, its style, the dance, liveliness, and the verb of making something livelier.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：爵士乐、其风格、爵士舞、活力，以及使更有生气的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trumpeter improvising while the drummer answers him.
core.cn: 核心意象：小号手即兴，鼓手在旁边回应。

branches.en: THE BANDS: brass, blues, and a rhythm section.
branches.cn: 乐队这条线：铜管、蓝调与节奏组。

branches.en: THE CAFE: dark wood and warm lights with no music playing.
branches.cn: 咖啡馆这条线：深木与暖灯，却不放音乐。

branches.en: THE STUDIO: dancers learning a swing step.
branches.cn: 舞蹈室这条线：学员模仿摇摆步。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a little colour that wakes it up.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：一点让人醒过来的颜色。

branches.en: THE MENU: ornaments added for a festival.
branches.cn: 菜单这条线：为节日添上的花样。

intro.en: Jazz is a modern American coinage or slang borrowing; the additions below are ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: jazz 是近代美国造词或俚语借词，下面的添加成分都是普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Jazz has no Latin source, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: jazz 没有拉丁语来源，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: It forms jazz band and jazz club.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jazz band 与 jazz club。

definition_zh: 标本；样本；样品
definition_en: a small part or example of something kept or tested to show what the whole is like
core_image: 玻璃罐里泡着一片叶子，标签上写着采集地点与日期
scene: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。 The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
sceneCN: 这里 specimen 是「标本」（第 1 个义项）；句意：科学家把一片叶子做成标本。

senses.title: A kept example
senses.definition: a part of a plant or animal kept for study
senses.definitionCN: 保存下来供研究的动植物部分
senses.example: The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。
senses.why: This is the museum and laboratory sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是博物馆和实验室里的含义。

senses.title: A sample for testing
senses.definition: a small amount taken to be tested or examined
senses.definitionCN: 取出用于检测或检查的少量物质
senses.example: The lab tested a blood specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室检测了一份血液样本。
senses.why: Anything taken for testing acts as a specimen.
senses.whyCN: 任何取出供检测的东西都充当样本。

senses.title: A type of person
senses.definition: a person considered as an example of a kind, often humorously
senses.definitionCN: 作为某类范例的人，常带幽默意味
senses.example: The coach called him a fine specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称他是个体格健壮的好苗子。
senses.why: Informal speech treats a strong person like a fine sample.
senses.whyCN: 口语把强壮的人比作上好的样本。

intro.en: Specimen is Latin for a mark or sample, from the verb to look.
intro.cn: specimen 是拉丁语中表示标记或样品的词，源于表示看的动词。

items.en: Specere meant to look or observe.
items.cn: specere 意为看或观察。

items.en: Specimen meant a mark or a sample to look at.
items.cn: specimen 意为标记或供观察的样品。

items.en: Specimen entered English as a sample for study.
items.cn: specimen 以研究样本之义进入英语。

items.en: Museums kept plant and animal specimens.
items.cn: 博物馆保存动植物标本。

items.en: Medicine took specimens for testing.
items.cn: 医学取样本进行检测。

note.en: Specimen is compared with look-alike words and words for samples.
note.cn: 把 specimen 与形近词以及表示样品的词作比较。

entries.definition: unusual or dedicated
entries.definitionCN: 特别的；专门的

entries.definition: to state exactly
entries.definitionCN: 明确说明

entries.definition: a biological group
entries.definitionCN: 物种

entries.definition: a small part taken as an example
entries.definitionCN: 样品

entries.definition: one thing that shows a group
entries.definitionCN: 例子

entries.definition: a small copy of something
entries.definitionCN: 模型

normalIntro.en: A specimen is a small piece kept so that others can look closely.
normalIntro.cn: specimen 是保留下来的小块，供人仔细观看。

normal.en: The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
normal.cn: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。

normal.en: The lab tested a blood specimen.
normal.cn: 实验室检测了一份血液样本。

normal.en: The coach called him a fine specimen.
normal.cn: 教练称他是个体格健壮的好苗子。

normal.en: The museum keeps rare specimens in glass cases.
normal.cn: 博物馆把稀有标本保存在玻璃柜里。

normal.en: She collected plant specimens on the walk.
normal.cn: 她在散步时采集了植物标本。

abstract.en: A specimen is a part that agrees to speak for the whole.
abstract.cn: 标本是愿意替整体发言的一部分。

abstract.en: To study a leaf is to question the forest.
abstract.cn: 研究一片叶子，就是在追问整片森林。

abstract.en: What is kept in glass is kept from living.
abstract.cn: 封在玻璃里的，也被挡在生命之外。

examples.en: The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
examples.cn: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。

examples.en: The lab tested a blood specimen.
examples.cn: 实验室检测了一份血液样本。

examples.en: The coach called him a fine specimen.
examples.cn: 教练称他是个体格健壮的好苗子。

dict_mnemonic.text: specimen 源自拉丁语 specere（看），指供观察研究的「标本、样本」；复数 specimens，blood specimen 是「血液样本」，specimen collection 是「标本收藏」，同根词有 species、specific、specify。

root: 来自拉丁语 specimen（标记、样品），源于 specere（看），本义为供人观察的东西，后指动植物标本、检测样本与某种类型的人。

sensesIntro.en: Specimen means a part kept for study, a sample for testing, or informally a type of person.
sensesIntro.cn: specimen 指保存供研究的标本、供检测的样本，或口语中某种类型的人。

core.en: A small piece offered to the eye.
core.cn: 呈给眼睛看的一小块。

branches.en: A leaf floats in a labelled jar.
branches.cn: 一片叶子浮在贴着标签的罐子里。

branches.en: A tube of blood goes to the lab.
branches.cn: 一管血被送往实验室。

branches.en: A strong young man is praised by his coach.
branches.cn: 教练称赞一个健壮的年轻人。

branches.en: Museum and laboratory both study small parts.
branches.cn: 博物馆与实验室都研究小部分。

branches.en: A sample for testing and a sample of a person share one image.
branches.cn: 检测样本与人的样本，共享一个意象。

intro.en: Specimen connects to the Latin family of looking.
intro.cn: specimen 与拉丁语中表示观看的词族相连。

latinIntro.en: The root is specimen, a sample, from specere, to look.
latinIntro.cn: 其词根是 specimen（样品），源于 specere（看）。

items.example: The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
items.exampleCN: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。

items.example: The museum keeps rare specimens in glass cases.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆把稀有标本保存在玻璃柜里。

items.example: This bird belongs to an endangered species.
items.exampleCN: 这种鸟属于一个濒危物种。

items.example: Please specify the date of your arrival on the form.
items.exampleCN: 请在表格上注明你到达的日期。

items.example: This book is written specifically for beginners.
items.exampleCN: 这本书是专为初学者写的。

definition_zh: 好奇心；稀奇的事物
definition_en: a strong wish to know or learn, or a strange and interesting thing
core_image: 一个孩子蹲在地上，盯着一只翻身的甲虫看很久
scene: 孩子蹲在地上，盯着一只翻身的甲虫看了很久。 Her curiosity made her open every drawer in the house.
sceneCN: 这里 curiosity 指「好奇心」（第 1 个义项：强烈想知道或学习的愿望）；句意是好奇心让她把家里每个抽屉都打开了。

senses.title: Wish to know
senses.definition: a strong wish to know or learn something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈想知道或了解某事的愿望
senses.example: Curiosity led her to ask questions all day.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心让她整天问问题。
senses.why: A mind that wants an answer will not sit still.
senses.whyCN: 想要答案的心，坐不住。

senses.title: A strange object
senses.definition: an object that is strange and interesting
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪而有趣的东西
senses.example: The shop sells old maps and curiosities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖旧地图和稀奇玩意儿。
senses.why: Things that do not fit the pattern get kept.
senses.whyCN: 不合常规的东西，会被留下来。

senses.title: Interest in others' affairs
senses.definition: an eagerness to know about other people's private lives
senses.definitionCN: 急于知道别人私事的愿望
senses.example: Her curiosity about the neighbours annoyed them.
senses.exampleCN: 她对邻居的好奇让他们不快。
senses.why: Not every question is welcome.
senses.whyCN: 并不是每个问题都受欢迎。

intro.en: Curiosity comes from Latin curiositas, the wish to know, from cura, care.
intro.cn: curiosity 源自拉丁语 curiositas（求知的愿望），其根是 cura（关心）。

items.en: Cura meant care and attention.
items.cn: cura 意为关心与用心。

items.en: Curiosus meant careful, then eager to know.
items.cn: curiosus 意为用心的，后来指急于知道。

items.en: Curiositas named the wish to learn.
items.cn: curiositas 指求知的愿望。

items.en: Curiosite kept the wish to know.
items.cn: curiosite 保留了求知的愿望。

items.en: Curiosity also named a rare object worth keeping.
items.cn: curiosity 也指值得收藏的稀奇物件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of interest in knowing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 词干，近义组列出其他想了解的说法。

entries.definition: wanting to know something
entries.definitionCN: 想知道某事的

entries.definition: in a curious way
entries.definitionCN: 以好奇或奇怪的方式

entries.definition: to make a sick person well
entries.definitionCN: 让病人康复

entries.definition: a wish to know more about something
entries.definitionCN: 想更多了解某事的愿望

entries.definition: a feeling of surprise and question
entries.definitionCN: 惊奇又带疑问的感受

entries.definition: a habit of asking many questions
entries.definitionCN: 爱问许多问题的习性

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a child and a beetle and end with a drawer pulled open.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从孩子与甲虫开始，落到被拉开的抽屉。

normal.en: Curiosity is care that will not let a question go.
normal.cn: 好奇心是不肯放过问题的关心。

normal.en: A child can watch one beetle for an hour.
normal.cn: 一个孩子能盯着一只甲虫看一小时。

normal.en: Every drawer in the house was opened once.
normal.cn: 家里每个抽屉都被打开过一次。

normal.en: The same word keeps old maps in a shop.
normal.cn: 同一个词也收着店里的旧地图。

normal.en: Curiosity about neighbours is often not welcome.
normal.cn: 对邻居的好奇，常常不受欢迎。

abstract.en: Picture a small face very close to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一张贴得很近地面的小脸。

abstract.en: Picture a finger lifting a stone to see what lives under it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指掀起石头，看下面住着什么。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of odd things with paper labels.
abstract.cn: 想象一架贴着纸标签的稀奇物件。

examples.en: Curiosity made him read the whole letter.
examples.cn: 好奇心让他读完了整封信。

examples.en: She asked, out of pure curiosity, where he had been.
examples.cn: 她纯粹出于好奇，问他去了哪里。

examples.en: The old shop is full of curiosities.
examples.cn: 这家老店满是稀奇玩意儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curiosity 记成「关心到非弄明白不可」：拉丁语 cura 是关心，往前一步就是好奇。

root: 源自拉丁语 curiositas（求知的愿望），其根是 cura（关心）；本义是用心探究，后指好奇心，也指因稀奇而被收藏的物件。

sensesIntro.en: From a wish to know, to a strange object, to interest in other people's lives.
sensesIntro.cn: 从想知道的愿望，到稀奇物件，再到对别人生活的兴趣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child crouching over a beetle, unwilling to leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子蹲在甲虫旁，舍不得走。

branches.en: A mind that needs the answer keeps asking.
branches.cn: 非要答案的心，会一直问下去。

branches.en: An odd object is kept because it raises questions.
branches.cn: 稀奇物件被留下，是因为它引出问题。

branches.en: The same pull can turn toward other people.
branches.cn: 同一股拉力，也会转向别人的生活。

branches.en: The wish to know and the odd thing feed each other.
branches.cn: 想知道的愿望与稀奇物件互相喂养。

branches.en: A collector and a gossip both follow curiosity.
branches.cn: 收藏者与爱打听的人，都跟着好奇心走。

intro.en: Curiosity belongs to the Latin cura family, with curious and cure close by.
intro.cn: curiosity 属于拉丁语 cura 一族，curious 与 cure 都在旁边。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cura, care, is the root that turned into curiosity and curious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura（关心）是变成 curiosity 与 curious 的根。

items.example: The child is curious about ants.
She looked curiously at the box.
items.exampleCN: 她好奇地看着那只箱子。

items.example: He was incurious about the world.

items.meaning: a shop selling odd old things
items.example: They found it in a curiosity shop.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一家旧货店找到它。

items.example: The museum began as a cabinet of curiosities.
items.exampleCN: 这座博物馆最初是一只珍奇柜。

definition_zh: 撤回；退出；取款；戒断（症状）；退缩
definition_en: the act of taking something back or out, of leaving a group, or of stopping a habit
core_image: 银行柜员把一叠现金数好，用橡皮筋一扎，从窗口那侧推到你面前
scene: 柜员把一叠现金数好扎紧，从窗口那侧推过来，纸上盖着取款日期。 The withdrawal of the offer left the whole team without a plan.
sceneCN: 这里 withdrawal 是「取款、撤回」（第 1 个义项：把钱或已提出之物拿回来这一行为）；句意为提议被撤回，整个团队一下子没了方案。柜员推过来的那叠现金，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Taking money out
senses.definition: the act of taking money out of a bank account
senses.definitionCN: 从银行账户中把钱取出的行为
senses.example: The withdrawal appeared on her statement the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 第二天早上，这笔取款就出现在她的账单上。
senses.why: The ending -al turns the verb into the act itself, so withdrawal is the pulling-out as a named event.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -al 把动词变成行为本身，所以 withdrawal 成了有名字的事件。

senses.title: Taking back an offer or support
senses.definition: the act of officially ending an offer, a promise or help you had given
senses.definitionCN: 正式结束自己曾给出的提议、承诺或帮助的行为
senses.example: The withdrawal of the offer left the whole team without a plan.
senses.exampleCN: 提议被撤回，整个团队一下子没了方案。
senses.why: What was given is pulled back, and the noun records that formal pulling back.
senses.whyCN: 所给予的被拉回，名词记录下这次正式的拉回。

senses.title: Leaving a contest or a group
senses.definition: the act of stopping your part in a competition, a treaty or an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 停止参与比赛、条约或组织的行为
senses.example: Its withdrawal from the agreement surprised its allies.
senses.exampleCN: 它退出协议让盟友们大为惊讶。
senses.why: Leaving is the same motion seen from outside: a side folds up and moves away.
senses.whyCN: 离开是同一动作从外部看到的样子：一方收起自己、走开。

senses.title: Stopping a habit
senses.definition: the process and the uncomfortable effects of stopping a substance your body is used to
senses.definitionCN: 停止使用身体已习惯之物时的过程及其不适反应
senses.example: He suffered headaches during the first days of withdrawal.
senses.exampleCN: 戒断的最初几天，他头痛得厉害。
senses.why: The body has grown used to a substance, and taking it away is literally a withdrawal from the body.
senses.whyCN: 身体已习惯了某种物质，把它拿走，字面上就是从身体里抽走。

intro.en: Withdrawal is withdraw plus the Latin-derived noun ending -al, which English borrowed for naming acts.
intro.cn: withdrawal 是 withdraw 加上源自拉丁语的 -al 词尾，英语借它来命名行为。

items.en: The verb was built from wið, away, and dragan, to pull.
items.cn: 这个动词由 wið（离开）与 dragan（拉）构成。

items.en: The verb spread from hands and weapons to promises and troops.
items.cn: 动词从手与武器扩展到承诺与军队。

items.en: The ending -al, borrowed through French, allowed the act to be named as a noun.
items.cn: 经由法语借来的词尾 -al，让这一行为能被命名成名词。

items.en: Banking made the money sense the commonest in daily life.
items.cn: 银行业让取款义成为日常生活中最常见的一个。

items.en: Medicine added the sense of stopping a drug, which spread into general speech.
items.cn: 医学又添加了戒药义，并扩展到日常语言。

note.en: The first group holds the verb and its neighbours, the second other nouns for leaving or taking back.
note.cn: 第一组收动词及其近邻，第二组收表示离开或收回的其他名词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 撤回；取款

entries.definition: Keeping something back from a person.
entries.definitionCN: 扣留

entries.definition: The act of reaching a place.
entries.definitionCN: 到达

entries.definition: The act of agreeing formally.
entries.definitionCN: 批准

entries.definition: A movement back from danger.
entries.definitionCN: 撤退

entries.definition: Formally stepping down from a post.
entries.definitionCN: 辞职

entries.definition: Money paid into an account.
entries.definitionCN: 存款

normalIntro.en: Withdrawal is the verb plus -al, exactly like arrival from arrive and approval from approve.
normalIntro.cn: withdrawal 就是动词加 -al，正如 arrive 变 arrival、approve 变 approval。

normal.en: Withdraw plus al, and the double r stays before the ending.
normal.cn: withdraw 加 al，末尾的 w 与元音之间保留一个 r。

normal.en: Same pattern as arrival and proposal: verbs turn into acts with -al.
normal.cn: 和 arrival、proposal 同一模式：动词加 -al 变成行为。

normal.en: Withdrawal symptoms put the body in a room it has just left.
normal.cn: 戒断症状让身体留在刚离开的那个房间里。

normal.en: Cash withdrawal is the phrase on every cash machine.
normal.cn: cash withdrawal 是每台取款机上都有的字样。

normal.en: Compare withhold and withdraw: one keeps, one pulls back.
normal.cn: 比较 withhold 与 withdraw：一个留住，一个拉回。

abstract.en: A stack of notes pushed through a slot.
abstract.cn: 一叠钞票被从窗口推出来。

abstract.en: A name crossed off a list of talks.
abstract.cn: 谈判名单上的一个名字被划掉。

abstract.en: An empty cup where there was always one before.
abstract.cn: 原本总有杯子在的地方，如今空了。

examples.en: There is a daily limit on cash withdrawals.
examples.cn: 取现每天有额度上限。

examples.en: The withdrawal of the team from the league was announced on Monday.
examples.cn: 球队退出联赛的消息在周一公布。

examples.en: Patience is needed during the withdrawal period.
examples.cn: 戒断期间需要耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: withdraw（撤回、取款）+ al（行为）—— 这个行为就叫「撤回、取款」。

root: with（离开）+ draw（拉）→ withdraw → withdraw + -al → withdrawal；同族有 withdrawn、withhold。

sensesIntro.en: A single act of pulling back appears as money from an account, an offer from the table, a group from a treaty, and a substance from a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个拉回的动作，表现为账户里的钱、桌上的提议、条约里的成员，以及身体里的药物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bundle of notes pushed across a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠钞票从柜台那侧推过来。

branches.en: The money branch: a line on the monthly statement.
branches.cn: 金钱分支：月账单上的一行。

branches.en: The offer branch: a team left without a plan.
branches.cn: 提议分支：失去方案的团队。

branches.en: The treaty branch: allies surprised by the news.
branches.cn: 条约分支：震惊的盟友。

branches.en: The body branch: headaches in the first days.
branches.cn: 身体分支：最初几天的头痛。

branches.en: The record branch: every withdrawal leaves a line behind.
branches.cn: 记录分支：每次撤回都会留下痕迹。

intro.en: Withdrawal is with- plus draw plus -al; the ending is the same one that turns arrive into arrival.
intro.cn: withdrawal 是 with- 加 draw 再加 -al；这个词尾与 arrive 变 arrival 所用的一致。

latinIntro.en: The ending -al came into English through French from Latin -alis; the Latin entries below show that borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -al 经法语从拉丁语 -alis 进入英语；下面的拉丁条目展示了这层借用。

items.example: The same prefix, a still hand.
items.exampleCN: 同一前缀，一只不动的手。

definition_zh: 误解；误会；理解错
definition_en: to take words, actions or intentions in a sense other than the one intended
core_image: 一句话从一只耳朵进去，绕了一圈，出来时已经换了意思
scene: 仓库里机器轰鸣，两个人隔着流水线喊话。 Above the noise of the machines he misunderstood the address and sent the parcel to the wrong depot.
sceneCN: 这里是「理解错对方的话」（第 1 个义项：把话里的意思听岔）；句意为机器声太吵，他把地址听错了，把包裹发去了另一个仓库。图中可辨识物件：流水线、包裹、写着地址的单据。

derivatives.zh: 由 misunderstand 加 -ing 构成，义为「误解；小争执」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「被误解的；不被理解的」

senses.title: To take spoken or written words in the wrong sense
senses.definition: to fail to get the meaning of what someone says or writes, so that the wrong sense is taken
senses.definitionCN: 没能正确领会别人说出或写下的意思，接住的是另一个意思
senses.example: I misunderstood the instructions and booked the later train.
senses.exampleCN: 我理解错了说明，订了晚一班的车。
senses.why: Understand began as a picture of standing close enough to a thing to grasp it; mis- says the standing happened in the wrong place, so the words are grasped from the wrong side.
senses.whyCN: understand 最早的画面是站得足够近、伸手能抓住某物；mis- 说明站错了位置，于是话语是从错的一侧被抓住的。

senses.title: To read behaviour or intention wrongly
senses.definition: to give a wrong explanation to someone's action, tone or motive
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的举动、语气或动机作出了错误的解释
senses.example: She misunderstood his silence and thought he was angry.
senses.exampleCN: 她误会了他的沉默，以为他在生气。
senses.why: Behaviour carries no words to pin it down, so the same verb is used when the mind supplies the wrong motive; the error moves from the sentence to the person behind it.
senses.whyCN: 行为没有字句可以钉住意思，于是当脑子给出错误的动机时，仍用同一个动词；错误从句子挪到了句子背后的人身上。

senses.title: To be understood wrongly by other people
senses.definition: to have one's meaning or character taken wrongly by others, used in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 自己的意思或为人被别人理解错了，多用被动形式
senses.example: He felt misunderstood by a family that never asked what he meant.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得家里人从不问他本意，因而误解了他。
senses.why: The passive turns the verb around: the person no longer does the misunderstanding but suffers it, and the word now names the gap between what was meant and what others heard.
senses.whyCN: 被动把动词倒了过来：不再是人去误解，而是人承受误解；这个词命名的正是「本意」与「别人听见的」之间那道缝。

intro.en: Misunderstand is an English-built verb: the Old English prefix for wrongly placed on the Old English verb for grasping a meaning.
intro.cn: misunderstand 是英语自己造的动词：把古英语中表示「错误地」的前缀，加在表示「领会」的古英语动词上。

items.en: The prefix mis- already meant wrongly or amiss in Old English and had long been used to mark failed or bad actions.
items.cn: 前缀 mis- 在古英语中就表示「错误地、不当」，早已用来标记失败或不当的动作。

items.en: Understandan began with the physical sense of standing in the midst of something and later came to mean grasping its meaning.
items.cn: understandan 最早是「站在某物之中」的具体意思，后来才转为领会它的含义。

items.en: The compound misunderstanden appears in the fifteenth century, first in the sense of taking a statement in the wrong way.
items.cn: 这个复合形式 misunderstanden 出现在十五世纪，最早指把一段话理解错了。

items.en: The verb widened to cover wrong readings of actions and motives, and the derived noun misunderstanding named both the error and the quarrel it caused.
items.cn: 到近代早期，这个动词扩大到指对行为与动机的错误解读；派生名词 misunderstanding 同时指错误本身和它引起的争执。

items.en: Modern English uses the passive be misunderstood for people whose meaning never reaches others, a sense that keeps the verb close to its image of failed contact.
items.cn: 现代英语用被动形式 be misunderstood 指本意没能传到别人那里的人；这一层仍贴着「接触失败」的原画面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the verb it was built on and its own derived forms plus the shared prefix; the near-meaning group holds verbs of hearing, reading and judging wrongly.
note.cn: 形近组收它赖以构成的动词、自身派生形式与共用的前缀；近义组收表示听错、读错、判断错的动词。

entries.definition: The noun and adjective from understand: the ability to grasp meaning, or a sympathetic person.
entries.definitionCN: 由 understand 来的名词与形容词，指领会能力，或指体谅人的。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb, also used as an adjective for someone whose meaning was not received.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词的过去形式，也作形容词指本意没被接住的人。

entries.definition: The prefix for wrongly, the part that turns understanding into misunderstanding.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「错误地」的前缀，正是它把领会变成了误解。

entries.definition: To explain or read something in a way that gives it the wrong meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物解释或解读成错误的意思。

entries.definition: To hear words wrongly, usually because of noise rather than because of the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 把话听错，多因噪声而非因意思难懂。

entries.definition: To take one thing for another in the mind, or to make someone unable to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 在心里把一物当成另一物，或让人听不明白。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a prefix of error and a verb whose first picture was standing close enough to grasp something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由一个表示错误的前缀，和一个最早表示「站近了抓住」的动词构成。

normal.en: Mis- is the same prefix that marks wrong actions across English, so misunderstand is simply to understand amiss.
normal.cn: mis- 是英语里标记错误动作的同一个前缀，所以 misunderstand 就是「领会歪了」。

normal.en: Understand first meant to stand in the midst of something, which is why the word for comprehension still feels like reaching and holding.
normal.cn: understand 最早指站在某物之中，所以这个表示「领会」的词至今仍像伸手去够、去握住。

normal.en: Misunderstood is both the past form and the state of someone whose point never landed.
normal.cn: misunderstood 既是过去形式，也是「本意从未落地」的那种状态。

normal.en: Misunderstanding names the failure and often the small quarrel that follows it.
normal.cn: misunderstanding 既指理解失败，也常指由此引起的小争执。

normal.en: Mishear is about the ear, misunderstand is about the sense, which is why one can mishear a word and still understand the sentence.
normal.cn: mishear 关涉耳朵，misunderstand 关涉意思；所以人可以听错一个词，却仍明白整句话。

abstract.en: Two people can use the same sentence and still live in different meanings, which is what this verb keeps recording.
abstract.cn: 两个人可以说同一句话，却住在不同的意思里；这个动词记录的就是这种情形。

abstract.en: The prefix marks the gap, not the blame: misunderstanding often happens where both sides were listening honestly.
abstract.cn: 前缀标出的是那道缝，而不是罪责；误解常常发生在双方都认真听的时候。

abstract.en: To feel misunderstood is to be sure of one's own meaning and unable to hand it over.
abstract.cn: 觉得被误解，就是确信自己的意思，却递不过去。

examples.en: I misunderstood the instructions and pressed the wrong button.
examples.cn: 我理解错了说明，按错了按钮。

examples.en: She misunderstood his silence as a refusal.
examples.cn: 她把他的沉默误会成了拒绝。

examples.en: He felt misunderstood by everyone at the office.
examples.cn: 他觉得办公室里的每个人都误解了他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷死俺的斯坦德」——听岔了还死守自己的理解，就是误解。

root: 由古英语前缀 mis-（错误地）加 understand（理解）构成；understand 源自古英语 understandan，本义「站在其中」，后转指领会。属英语自造词，无可靠拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is failed contact with a meaning; the senses run from misheard words to misread behaviour and finally to the person whose meaning never arrives.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没能接住意思」；义项从听错的话，走到读错的行为，最后走到本意始终没能送达的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence entering one ear, looping around, and coming out with a different meaning.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话从一只耳朵进去，绕了一圈，出来时已经换了意思。

branches.en: an address taken down wrongly in a noisy workshop
branches.cn: 嘈杂车间里被记错的地址

branches.en: a silent man read as an angry one
branches.cn: 沉默的人被读成生气的人

branches.en: a speaker whose point never reached the others
branches.cn: 观点始终没能传到对方那里的说话人

branches.en: a message retold with a changed tone
branches.cn: 被转述时走了调的话

branches.en: a family talking past each other at one table
branches.cn: 同一张桌上各说各话的一家人

intro.en: The word combines a prefix of error, a verb built on standing, and English endings that produce the noun and the passive adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示错误的前缀、一个以「站立」为本的动词，以及造出名词与被动形容词的英语词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for misunderstand; both the prefix and the verb are native English stock of Germanic origin.
latinIntro.cn: misunderstand 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；前缀与动词都是日耳曼来源的英语本族成分。
