a failure to understand, or a small quarrel

definition_zh: 摄影术；摄影；摄影业
definition_en: the art, process or business of taking and producing photographs
core_image: 暗房的红灯下，一张白纸在药水里慢慢浮出树影
scene: 暗房里只有一盏红灯，夹子把湿漉漉的相纸从药水里提起来，树影一点点显出来。 Photography began as chemistry before it became an art.
sceneCN: 这里是「摄影术」（第 1 个义项：拍摄与成像的技艺）；句意为摄影在成为艺术之前，先是一门化学。红灯、药水和慢慢显影的相纸正是这门技艺的现场。

derivatives.zh: photo- 加 -graph 再加 -er，义为「摄影师」；与 -graphy 只差一个结尾
photo- 加 -genic（产生），义为「上相的」
astro-（星）加 photography，义为「天文摄影」

senses.title: The art and process of making images with light
senses.definition: the art and process of recording images by the action of light on film or on a sensor
senses.definitionCN: 利用光在胶片或传感器上成像、从而记录画面的技艺与过程
senses.example: Photography began as chemistry before it became an art.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影在成为艺术之前，先是一门化学。
senses.why: -graphy names a practice rather than a thing: the same Greek base that gives the picture also gives the skill of making pictures once the ending shifts to -y.
senses.whyCN: -graphy 指一种做法而不是一件东西：同一个希腊词干，结尾换成 -y，就从「照片」变成「拍照片的技艺」。

senses.title: The trade built on that practice
senses.definition: the business or activity of producing photographs, especially for clients or publications
senses.definitionCN: 为客户或出版物拍摄、制作照片的行业或活动
senses.example: She moved to Milan to work in fashion photography.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬到米兰从事时尚摄影。
senses.why: Abstract craft nouns regularly extend to the trade that lives off them, and photography followed printing and painting along the same path.
senses.whyCN: 表示技艺的抽象名词常会扩展到靠它吃饭的行当；photography 沿着 printing、painting 走过的同一条路延伸。

intro.en: Photography names a practice, and its history runs from a Greek suffix for writing through a French coinage of the 1830s to a global industry.
intro.cn: photography 命名一门技艺，它的历史从希腊语表示「书写」的后缀，经十九世纪三十年代的法语新造词，一直走到今天的全球行业。

items.en: Phos, genitive photos, meant light and supplied the first element of the compound.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光，提供了复合词的第一部分。

items.en: Graphein meant to draw or write; the derived noun graphia named a writing, a drawing or a record.
items.cn: graphein 意为画、写；由它派生的名词 graphia 指书写、图画或记录。

items.en: Hercules Florence used photographie in 1834, and the word spread with the processes that Daguerre and Talbot made public in 1839.
items.cn: 埃尔屈勒·弗洛朗斯在 1834 年使用了 photographie；随着达盖尔与塔尔博特在 1839 年公布新工艺，这个词传播开来。

items.en: English kept -graph for the image, -er for the person and -y for the practice, a division that still explains the whole family.
items.cn: 英语保留 -graph 指影像、-er 指人、-y 指技艺，这个分工至今仍能解释整族词。

items.en: Digital sensors replaced film, but photography still covers the art, the course of study and the industry, with compounds such as astrophotography extending it.
items.cn: 数码传感器取代了胶片，但 photography 仍兼指艺术、学科与行业，astrophotography 这类复合词继续扩展它的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group lines up the same Greek family so the endings can be compared; the near-meaning group collects other crafts that produce images.
note.cn: 形近组把同一希腊词族的成员排在一起，便于比较结尾；近义组收其他生产影像的技艺。

entries.definition: One image, ending in -graph; the practice word ends in -y instead.
entries.definitionCN: 一张影像，结尾是 -graph；指技艺的词结尾则是 -y。

entries.definition: The person who practises it, ending in -er.
entries.definitionCN: 从事这门技艺的人，结尾是 -er。

entries.definition: The adjective describing materials, methods or effects of the craft.
entries.definitionCN: 描述这门技艺的材料、方法或效果的形容词。

entries.definition: Likely to look good in a photograph, built with -genic.
entries.definitionCN: 适合上镜、拍照好看的，由 -genic 构成。

entries.definition: The craft of photographing films, where -graphy also names a technique.
entries.definitionCN: 电影拍摄的技艺；这里的 -graphy 同样指一门技术。

entries.definition: The way a camera is used in a film or television programme.
entries.definitionCN: 影视作品中运用摄影机的方式。

entries.definition: The technical process of producing images, especially digital ones.
entries.definitionCN: 生成图像的技术过程，尤指数字成像。

normalIntro.en: The word is a practice noun, and its -graphy ending is the same one that turns other roots into crafts and fields of study.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示技艺的名词，它的 -graphy 结尾与把其他词根变成手艺、学科时用的是同一个。

normal.en: -graphy comes from Greek -graphia, a writing or a record, so photography is writing with light.
normal.cn: -graphy 来自希腊语 -graphia，意为书写或记录，所以 photography 就是用光书写。

normal.en: -graph is the picture, -grapher the person, -graphy the practice; only the last letters change.
normal.cn: -graph 是照片，-grapher 是人，-graphy 是技艺；变的只是最后几个字母。

normal.en: The -y ending makes an uncountable noun of a skill, as it does in geography and calligraphy.
normal.cn: -y 结尾把技能变成不可数名词，geography 和 calligraphy 也是这样。

normal.en: Photography covers both the art and the industry, so a photography course can lead to a photography business.
normal.cn: photography 兼指艺术与行业，所以摄影课程可以通向一门摄影生意。

normal.en: Digital sensors replaced film, but a sensor still counts light, so the photo- half remains accurate.
normal.cn: 数码传感器取代了胶片，但传感器仍在计量光，所以 photo- 那一半依然准确。

abstract.en: Photography is a bargain with time: it keeps a moment but never the moment itself.
abstract.cn: 摄影是与时间做的一笔交易：它留住一个瞬间，却从不是那个瞬间本身。

abstract.en: -graphy turns an action into a discipline, which is why the word sounds like something you can study.
abstract.cn: -graphy 把动作变成一门学科，所以这个词听起来像可以选修的科目。

abstract.en: A craft named after light and writing keeps both halves visible every time a print appears in the tray.
abstract.cn: 一门以光与书写命名的技艺，每次相纸在托盘里显影，都让这两半同时可见。

examples.en: Photography began as chemistry before it became an art.
examples.cn: 摄影在成为艺术之前，先是一门化学。

examples.en: She moved to Milan to work in fashion photography.
examples.cn: 她搬到米兰从事时尚摄影。

examples.en: Digital photography made the darkroom optional but not extinct.
examples.cn: 数码摄影让暗房不再是必需，却没有让它消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头格拉菲」——用光写字的手艺；记住 photography 是摄影术，结尾 -graphy 指技艺。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ graphein（写）+ 希腊名词后缀 -ia（英语作 -y）；-graph 指成品，-grapher 指人，-graphy 指书写、记录的技艺。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the practice of writing with light; one sense names the art and process, the other the trade that grew out of it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是用光书写的技艺；一个义项指这门艺术与过程，另一个指由它生长出来的行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a print rising out of a tray of developer under a red darkroom lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗房红灯下，一张相纸从显影液里慢慢浮出画面。

branches.en: a red lamp over a tray of developer
branches.cn: 显影液上方的一盏红灯

branches.en: a student learning exposure in a first course
branches.cn: 入门课上练习曝光的学生

branches.en: a studio booking a shoot for a fashion brand
branches.cn: 为时尚品牌安排拍摄的摄影棚

branches.en: an amateur habit turning into a paid trade
branches.cn: 从业余爱好变成收费行当

branches.en: pages of a magazine paid for by the shoot
branches.cn: 杂志上由这次拍摄换来的版面

intro.en: The word combines a Greek element for light with the Greek suffix for a craft, and the same suffix organises the whole family.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊语表示「光」的成分与表示技艺的希腊语后缀结合，同一个后缀也组织了整族词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的词根是希腊语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: forms nouns of practice or study
items.meaningCN: 构成表示技艺、学科的名词

items.meaning: the person who writes or draws

definition_zh: 不情愿的；勉强的；抗拒的
definition_en: not willing to do something and therefore slow to do it
core_image: 脚往前迈，身子却往后用力挣
scene: 父亲被劝了三次，才慢慢把手伸向那台新手机。 My father was reluctant to try the new phone, and it took three attempts to persuade him.
sceneCN: 这里 reluctant 是「不情愿的」（第 1 个义项：不愿意并因此拖延）；句意：父亲不愿意尝试那部新手机，劝了三次才说服他。

pos.zh: 不情愿的；勉强的；抗拒的

derivatives.zh: reluctant 加 -ance 构成，义为「不情愿；勉强」
reluctant 加 -ly 构成，义为「不情愿地」

senses.title: Unwilling and slow to act
senses.definition: not wanting to do something and therefore hesitating or delaying
senses.definitionCN: 不想做某事，因而犹豫或拖延
senses.example: She was reluctant to lend her car to a stranger.
senses.exampleCN: 她不愿意把车借给陌生人。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to struggle against, so the core picture is a body pulled forward while something inside pulls back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「挣扎反抗」，所以核心画面是身体被往前拉，内心却在往后挣。

senses.title: Shown in a forced or half-hearted way
senses.definition: done or given without real willingness, so it looks strained
senses.definitionCN: 并非真心愿意地做出或给出，因而显得勉强
senses.example: He gave a reluctant smile and turned away.
senses.exampleCN: 他勉强笑了笑，转过身去。
senses.why: When the inner struggle shows on the face, the adjective moves from the feeling to the visible expression.
senses.whyCN: 当内心的挣扎写在脸上，这个形容词就从描述感受转为描述可见的表情。

senses.title: Struggling against something
senses.definition: physically or inwardly resisting a force, now a rare and literary use
senses.definitionCN: 在身体或内心里抵抗某种力量，如今属少见且偏文学性的用法
senses.example: The reluctant horse refused to enter the water.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹抗拒的马不肯下水。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word, where the struggle is literal rather than a matter of unwillingness.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层，挣扎是字面意义上的，而不只是「不愿意」。

intro.en: Reluctant comes from the Latin present participle reluctans, from the verb reluctari.
intro.cn: reluctant 来自拉丁语现在分词 reluctans，源自动词 reluctari。

items.en: Reluctari means to struggle against or resist, built from re- and luctari, to wrestle.
items.cn: reluctari 意为奋力反抗，由 re- 与 luctari「摔跤、搏斗」构成。

items.en: Luctari is the verb behind luctatio, a wrestling match.
items.cn: luctari 是表示摔跤比赛的 luctatio 背后的动词。

items.en: The participle reluctans describes someone actively struggling back.
items.cn: 分词 reluctans 描述正在用力往回挣的人。

items.en: English borrows reluctant first in the literal sense of struggling against.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪先借入其「奋力抵抗」的字面义。

items.en: The word settles into the milder everyday sense of unwilling and hesitant.
items.cn: 这个词后来固定为更温和的日常义：不愿意、犹豫。

note.en: Reluctant belongs to a small family of unwillingness, and its Latin root is about wrestling.
note.cn: reluctant 属于表示「不愿意」的小词族，其拉丁词根与摔跤有关。

entries.definition: the feeling of not wanting to do something
entries.definitionCN: 不情愿；勉强，是 reluctant 的名词形式

entries.definition: in an unwilling way
entries.definitionCN: 不情愿地，由 reluctant 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: to struggle against, an obsolete verb
entries.definitionCN: 反抗；挣扎，是已废弃的动词，与 reluctant 同源

entries.definition: not wanting to do something
entries.definitionCN: 不愿意的，最直白的同义表达

entries.definition: slow to act or speak because of doubt
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫的，强调拿不定主意

entries.definition: given or done unwillingly and with bad grace
entries.definitionCN: 勉强的；不情愿的，带有抱怨意味

normalIntro.en: The Latin root luctari means to wrestle, so the word pictures an inner tug of war.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 luctari 意为「摔跤」，所以这个词画的是一场内心的拔河。

normal.en: Re- plus luctari, to wrestle, gives the picture of wrestling back against a pull.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 luctari「摔跤」，画面是朝着拉力反方向摔回去。

normal.en: The noun reluctance adds -ance, and the adverb reluctantly adds -ly.
normal.cn: 名词 reluctance 加 -ance，副词 reluctantly 加 -ly。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is be reluctant to do something.
normal.cn: 固定句型是 be reluctant to do something。

normal.en: A reluctant hero is someone who never wanted the role in the first place.
normal.cn: a reluctant hero 指从一开始就不想要这个角色的人。

normal.en: Reluctant and reluctance stress the second syllable, re-LUC-tant.
normal.cn: reluctant 与 reluctance 的重音在第二音节，读作 re-LUC-tant。

abstract.en: Imagine a dog bracing its paws while the leash pulls forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条狗四爪撑地，而牵引绳却往前拉。

abstract.en: See a child holding a door frame on the way to bed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子被带去睡觉时死死抓住门框。

abstract.en: Think of a smile that arrives half a second too late.
abstract.cn: 想一个慢了半拍才出现的笑容。

examples.en: Many people are reluctant to talk about money.
examples.cn: 许多人不愿意谈论钱。

examples.en: After a long pause she gave a reluctant nod.
examples.cn: 沉默良久，她勉强点了点头。

examples.en: The committee was reluctant to approve the plan.
examples.cn: 委员会不愿批准这项计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞拉克坦」——想象坦克不肯往前开，车组用力拉也不动；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 reluctari（反抗、挣扎），由 re-（反）+ luctari（摔跤）构成，现在分词 reluctans 即「正在反抗的」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a physical struggle, then narrows into the feeling of not wanting to act and the look that feeling produces.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指身体上的挣扎，后来收窄为「不想行动」的感受，以及这种感受在脸上留下的样子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet moving forward while the body pulls back.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚往前迈，身子却往后挣。

branches.en: Resistance felt inside becomes unwillingness and delay.
branches.cn: 内心的抵抗转化为不情愿与拖延。

branches.en: The struggle shows on the face as a strained smile or nod.
branches.cn: 挣扎写在脸上，就成了勉强的笑或点头。

branches.en: The oldest layer keeps the struggle literal, as a horse refusing water.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层保留字面的挣扎，例如马拒绝下水。

branches.en: The inner reluctance and its visible form are the same struggle.
branches.cn: 内心的不情愿与外在的勉强表现是同一种挣扎。

branches.en: Both describe a force meeting a counter-force.
branches.cn: 两者都描述一股力量遇到反向的力量。

intro.en: Reluctant is a Latin participle with a prefix, a root, and a present-participle ending.
intro.cn: reluctant 是拉丁分词，含前缀、词根与现在分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Re- means back, luctari means to wrestle, and -ant marks the person doing it.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「反、回」，luctari 表示「摔跤」，词尾 -ant 标记正在做这件事的人。

items.example: Re- turns the wrestling back against the pull.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 让这场摔跤朝拉力反方向进行。

items.example: The luct- root survives in the rare English word luctation.
items.exampleCN: luct- 词根残存在英语罕用词 luctation 中。

items.example: The ending -ant marks the person who is struggling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 标记正在挣扎的那个人。

items.example: Luctari is the verb at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: luctari 是这个词的核心动词。
reluctari 在 luctari 前加了 re-。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: Reluctance turns the adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: reluctance 把形容词变成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Luctation is a rare word that keeps the Latin root visible.
items.exampleCN: luctation 是保留拉丁词根原貌的罕用词。

definition_zh: 有影响力的；有势力的；有很大影响的
definition_en: having the power to affect people, decisions or events
core_image: 一个人说话，满屋子的人立刻改变主意
scene: 小镇上的报纸没人敢小看。 The local paper has become influential far beyond the town.
sceneCN: 这里 influential 是「有影响力的」（第 1 个义项：能影响他人或决定）；句意是这家地方报纸的影响力已远及镇外。

pos.zh: 形容词：有影响力的；有势力的；有很大影响的

derivatives.zh: 加否定前缀，义为「无影响力的」
同根词，义为「流行性感冒」

senses.title: Able to affect people
senses.definition: able to change how others think or act
senses.definitionCN: 能改变他人的想法或行为
senses.example: She became one of the most influential teachers in the school.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了学校里最有影响力的老师之一。
senses.why: The -ial ending simply turns influence into a quality someone has.
senses.whyCN: -ial 词尾只是把 influence 变成某人所具备的性质。

senses.title: Able to affect decisions
senses.definition: having power in politics, business or public life
senses.definitionCN: 在政治、商业或公共生活中拥有力量
senses.example: The committee is influential in local politics.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会在地方政治中很有影响力。
senses.why: Power over outcomes, not just opinions, is the second step.
senses.whyCN: 对结果而不只是对意见的支配力，是这个形容词的第二步。

senses.title: A work that shaped others
senses.definition: said of a book, idea or event that changed a whole field
senses.definitionCN: 指改变了整个领域的书、思想或事件
senses.example: This was an influential book on how children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一本关于儿童如何学习的深有影响的书。
senses.why: Things can carry influence too, especially works that others follow.
senses.whyCN: 事物也能携带影响力，尤其是被后人效仿的作品。

senses.title: Having many connections
senses.definition: having wealth or friends who can make things happen
senses.definitionCN: 拥有财富或能办事的人脉
senses.example: His family is influential in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他家在城里很有势力。
senses.why: From real effect the word slides to social weight and connections.
senses.whyCN: 从实际作用出发，这个词滑向社会分量与人脉。

intro.en: Influential is an English adjective formed on influence, from Medieval Latin influentia, a flowing in.
intro.cn: influential 是在 influence 上构成的英语形容词，后者出自中世纪拉丁语 influentia（流入）。

items.en: Influere meant to flow into, from in- plus fluere, to flow.
items.cn: influere 意为流入，由 in- 加 fluere（流动）构成。

items.en: Influentia named the invisible power believed to flow from the stars.
items.cn: influentia 指人们相信从星辰流入的无形力量。

items.en: The noun reached English through French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个名词在十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ial was attached to make an adjective in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪加上后缀 -ial 构成形容词。

items.en: Influential spread widely with talk of influential people and papers in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪谈有影响的人物与报纸，influential 广泛流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fluere family; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of power.
note.cn: 形近组收 fluere 词族；近义组收表示力量与地位的形容词。

entries.definition: The power to affect others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「影响」，是本词的来源。

entries.definition: A virus that once was blamed on the stars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流感」，同出意大利语 influenza。

entries.definition: In a way that has effect.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有影响地」。

entries.definition: Having great power.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强大的」，更笼统。

entries.definition: Of great value or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「重要的」，不必然指影响他人。

entries.definition: Large enough to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「显著的」，强调分量。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the adjective to its noun and to the flowing picture behind both.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把形容词与它的名词以及背后的流水画面相连。

normal.en: Influence plus -ial gives an adjective: full of influence.
normal.cn: influence 加 -ial 得形容词：充满影响力的。

normal.en: Influential is almost always used of people, papers and books, not of weather.
normal.cn: influential 几乎总用于人、报纸与书，而不用来形容天气。

normal.en: Influential in politics means able to steer decisions.
normal.cn: influential in politics 意为能左右决策。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the -flu- of flow, so the word still sounds like water.
normal.cn: 拼写保留流动的 -flu-，这个词听起来仍像水。

normal.en: More influential and most influential handle the comparison.
normal.cn: more influential 与 most influential 承担比较级与最高级。

abstract.en: An influential person is a river others quietly follow.
abstract.cn: 有影响力的人是一条别人默默顺着走的河。

abstract.en: Influence is measured backwards: we see it only in what changed.
abstract.cn: 影响力的度量是回望的：我们只在改变了的东西里看见它。

abstract.en: The word means pouring in, and power that pours never stays in one place.
abstract.cn: 这个词意为灌入，而倾注的力量从不只停在一处。

examples.en: He was an influential member of the committee.
examples.cn: 他是委员会里很有影响力的成员。

examples.en: The report proved influential in changing the law.
examples.cn: 这份报告在改变法律方面被证明很有影响。

examples.en: Few writers have been as influential as she was.
examples.cn: 很少有作家像她那样影响深远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因福露恩少」——因为福气与恩情露得少，才更要靠影响力说话。

root: influence（影响）+ -ial（形容词后缀）；词根为拉丁 fluere（流动）。

sensesIntro.en: Influential turns the flowing-in power into a quality: able to change people, then decisions, then whole fields, and finally social weight.
sensesIntro.cn: influential 把流入的力量变成一种性质：能改变人，然后是决策、整个领域，最后是社会分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker who changes the room in one sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话就让满屋转向的发言者。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: able to change minds.
branches.cn: 人际线：能改变人心。

branches.en: DECISION LINE: able to steer outcomes.
branches.cn: 决策线：能左右结果。

branches.en: WORKS LINE: books and ideas that reshape a field.
branches.cn: 作品线：重塑一个领域的书与思想。

branches.en: STATUS LINE: wealth and connections that carry weight.
branches.cn: 地位线：有分量的财富与人脉。

branches.en: POWER LINE: one unseen force, two directions.
branches.cn: 力量线：同一股无形之力，两个方向。

intro.en: An adjective in -ial formed on the noun of flowing in.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ial 结尾、由「流入」名词构成的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The root fluere, to flow, gives fluent, fluid, flux and influenza.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fluere（流动）产生 fluent、fluid、flux 与 influenza。

definition_zh: 哨子；口哨；哨声；吹口哨；鸣笛
definition_en: a small tube of metal or plastic blown to make a sharp sound, and the sound or the act of blowing through pursed lips
core_image: 裁判把银色小哨子含在嘴里，腮帮子一鼓，一声长响划过球场
scene: 球赛最后几秒，裁判把哨子举到嘴边用力吹了一下，全场忽然安静下来。 The referee blew the whistle and pointed at the penalty spot.
sceneCN: 这里 whistle 是「哨子」（第 1 个义项：用嘴吹出尖锐声音的小管）；句意为裁判吹响哨子并指向点球点。银色小哨与划破空气的一声长响，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The small blowing instrument
senses.definition: a small device, often metal or plastic, that makes a loud high sound when air is forced through it
senses.definitionCN: 一种小巧的器具，多为金属或塑料制成，用力吹气时发出响亮的高音
senses.example: The referee blew the whistle and pointed at the penalty spot.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判吹响哨子，指向点球点。
senses.why: The instrument is named by the sound it makes, so the object and its noise share one word.
senses.whyCN: 这个器具是以它发出的声音命名的，所以器具与声音共用一个词。

senses.title: The sound made by lips
senses.definition: the clear musical sound produced by forcing breath through a small round opening of the lips
senses.definitionCN: 把嘴唇收成小圆口、用力呼气而发出的清亮乐音
senses.example: A long whistle came from the boy on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 墙头上的男孩打了一声长长的口哨。
senses.why: Whistling with the lips needs no tool, yet it copies the same pipe of the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 用嘴唇吹口哨不需要任何工具，但它模仿的正是哨子那根小管。

senses.title: To make a whistling sound
senses.definition: to make a high sound by blowing through the lips or through an instrument, often to call or warn
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇或乐器发出高音，常用来呼叫或示警
senses.example: He whistled to his dog across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他在田野那头对着狗吹了一声口哨。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the sound into action, whether through lips, a train funnel or a kettle.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把声音变成动作，无论发声的是嘴唇、火车汽笛还是水壶。

senses.title: To move with a rushing sound
senses.definition: to travel very fast with a sound like wind forced through a narrow gap
senses.definitionCN: 快速移动，并发出像风挤过窄缝一样的声音
senses.example: A bullet whistled past his ear and buried itself in the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗子弹呼啸着擦过他的耳朵，钻进树里。
senses.why: Fast air through a thin gap makes exactly the pipe sound, so the word spread to anything rushing by.
senses.whyCN: 快速的气流穿过细缝时，发出的正是哨管般的声音，于是这个词扩展到一切疾驰而过之物。

senses.title: To reveal a secret to the police
senses.definition: in the phrase blow the whistle, to report wrongdoing inside an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在 blow the whistle 这一说法中，指揭发机构内部的违法行为
senses.example: She was the first to whistle on the fake receipts.
senses.exampleCN: 她是第一个举报假发票的人。
senses.why: A referee stops the game with a whistle, and a reporter stops a crime the same way in this image.
senses.whyCN: 裁判用哨声叫停比赛，而举报者用同样的画面叫停一桩罪行。

intro.en: Whistle is an imitative word: Old English hwistle named both the pipe and the sound, likely copying the hiss of air through a narrow hole.
intro.cn: whistle 是拟声词：古英语 hwistle 同时指那根哨管和它发出的声音，很可能是模仿气流穿过窄孔时的嘶声。

items.en: hwistle was the noun for a pipe or flute, and the verb hwistlian meant to make that sound.
items.cn: hwistle 指哨管或笛子，动词 hwistlian 表示发出这种声音。

items.en: The initial h was pronounced before the w, as in many old English words of that shape.
items.cn: 这个词开头的 h 在 w 之前发音，许多这一形状的古英语词都如此。

items.en: The h fell silent and the spelling moved towards whistle, while the meaning widened to lips and to birds.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 h 不再发音，拼写移向 whistle，词义也扩展到用嘴唇与鸟类。

items.en: Steam engines and kettles added the sense of a mechanical warning, and trains whistled at crossings.
items.cn: 蒸汽机与水壶带来了机械警示之义，火车在道口鸣笛。

items.en: Since the late twentieth century to blow the whistle has meant to expose wrongdoing inside an organization.
items.cn: 二十世纪末以来，blow the whistle 被用来表示揭发机构内部的违法行为。

note.en: The first group gathers other small wind instruments and their sounds, the second the acts of calling out or revealing something.
note.cn: 第一组收其他吹奏小乐器及其声音，第二组收呼喊与揭发一类动作。

entries.definition: A long thin pipe held sideways and played with the fingers.
entries.definitionCN: 长笛

entries.definition: A hollow instrument sounded by breath, louder and lower.
entries.definitionCN: 号角；喇叭

entries.definition: A loud device on a vehicle that wails as a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 警报器

entries.definition: A tube you blow into, the physical body of a whistle.
entries.definitionCN: 管子；哨管；笛

entries.definition: To make a long hollow call, as an owl or a horn does.
entries.definitionCN: 鸣叫；鸣笛

entries.definition: To give a sign that something should start or stop.
entries.definitionCN: 发信号

entries.definition: To bring a hidden wrong into the open, as a whistle-blower does.
entries.definitionCN: 揭发；揭露

normalIntro.en: Whistle is a sound word, so it is best fixed by hearing one rather than by staring at the letters.
normalIntro.cn: whistle 是个声音词，记住它最好的办法是听一声，而不是盯着字母看。

normal.en: The letters w h i s p e r are close to whisper, a sound made with almost no voice.
normal.cn: whistle 与 whisper 长得很像，后者是用几乎不带嗓音的口型发出的声音。

normal.en: A whistle is a pipe you blow, so picture a tiny tube rather than a person.
normal.cn: 哨子是你吹的那根小管，所以要想一根小管，而不是一个人。

normal.en: The referee, the kettle, the train and the bird all use the same sharp note.
normal.cn: 裁判、水壶、火车和鸟，用的是同一个尖锐的音。

normal.en: To blow the whistle is to stop the play of a dishonest office.
normal.cn: blow the whistle 就是叫停一间不诚实办公室里的那场比赛。

normal.en: The -le ending makes a light ending note, just as the sound dies away.
normal.cn: 词尾的 -le 像一声轻巧的收尾，正如声音渐渐散去。

abstract.en: Hear a flat high note cutting the noise of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 听见一个平直的高音切开人群的嘈杂。

abstract.en: Feel the small round hole of the lips holding the air back.
abstract.cn: 感觉嘴唇的小圆口把气暂时憋住。

abstract.en: Watch a dog turn its head before the sound has ended.
abstract.cn: 看那只狗在声音还没停时就已经转过头。

examples.en: The referee blew his whistle and the game restarted.
examples.cn: 裁判吹响哨子，比赛重新开始。

examples.en: She whistled softly while washing the dishes.
examples.cn: 她一边洗碗一边轻轻吹口哨。

examples.en: The wind whistled through the broken window all night.
examples.cn: 整夜风都从破窗里呼呼地响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威哨」——威力十足的哨子，一吹整条街都听见。

root: 拟声词：古英语 hwistle（哨管、笛，兼指其声）→ 中古英语 whistle → 现代英语 whistle；同族有 whistler、whistle-blower。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as the little pipe and its sound, widens from lips to machines, slides into the rushing sound of fast movement, and finally becomes the image of exposing a secret.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从哨管与哨声出发，由嘴唇扩展到机械，再滑向疾驰而过的呼啸声，最后成为揭发秘密的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver pipe held between two lips, one long high note.
core.cn: 核心意象：两片嘴唇之间的一支银色小管，一声高而长的音。

branches.en: The object branch: the referee points at the penalty spot.
branches.cn: 器物分支：裁判指向点球点。

branches.en: The sound branch: a long call from the boy on the wall.
branches.cn: 声音分支：墙头男孩发出的一声长哨。

branches.en: The action branch: whistling a dog home across a field.
branches.cn: 动作分支：在田野那头用口哨唤狗回家。

branches.en: The rushing branch: a bullet passing the ear.
branches.cn: 呼啸分支：一颗子弹擦过耳边。

branches.en: The exposing branch: stopping the play with a report.
branches.cn: 揭发分支：用一纸举报叫停比赛。

intro.en: Whistle is an imitation of sound rather than a built form, yet it takes the usual verb endings and appears inside compounds such as whistle-blower.
intro.cn: whistle 是声音的模仿而非构造成分，但它能带普通动词词尾，并出现在 whistle-blower 这类复合词中。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and imitative, so it has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below belong to borrowed relatives only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语的拟声词，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目只是借入的相关词。

items.example: It is the plain base form.
items.exampleCN: 它就是朴素的词根形式。

items.example: It makes the word sound like a small flute.
items.exampleCN: 它让这个词听起来像一支小笛子。

items.meaning: a person who reports a wrong
items.example: The compound keeps the referee image.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了裁判的形象。

items.meaning: a small station where a train waits briefly
items.example: The train sound names the halt itself.
items.exampleCN: 火车声给这个停靠点命了名。

items.meaning: a silent call for dogs, or a coded hint
items.meaningCN: 唤狗的无形哨；隐语暗号
items.example: The image moved from dogs to politics.
items.exampleCN: 这个形象从狗延伸到了政治。

latinEntries.example: Its hiss is the same narrow-air sound.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它嘶嘶的气流声正是同一种窄缝声。

definition_zh: 观察者；观测人员；旁观者；列席观察员
definition_en: a person who watches or records something, especially for research, or an onlooker who takes no part in an event
core_image: 教室最后一排坐着一个人，只在本子上记录，从不举手，也不打断任何事
scene: 培训教室里，一位列席者坐在最后一排，只在本子上记录，从不打断讲课。 The observer sat at the back and wrote down how often the teacher paused.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：只观看与记录、不参与其中的人；句意为这位观察者坐在后排，记下老师停顿的次数。图中可辨识物件：后排座位、记录本、秒表、讲台；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察者；观测员；旁观者；列席观察员（可数）

senses.title: A watcher who takes no part
senses.definition: a person who watches an event without joining in or changing it
senses.definitionCN: 观看事件、但不参与也不改变它的人
senses.example: The observer sat at the back and wrote down how often the teacher paused.
senses.exampleCN: 这位观察者坐在后排，记下老师停顿的次数。
senses.why: The word is built from the verb of watching plus the agent ending, so the person is defined by attention rather than action.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示观看的动词加施事词尾构成，因此这个人是被「注意」而非「行动」定义的。

senses.title: The recorder in a study
senses.definition: a researcher who watches and records behaviour or readings as part of a study
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究的一部分，观看并记录行为或读数的人
senses.example: A second observer checked the timings independently.
senses.exampleCN: 第二位观察者独立核对了计时。
senses.why: Two people watching the same session can compare notes, which is how a study shows that its records are reliable.
senses.whyCN: 两个人看同一场活动可以互相比对记录，研究正是以此证明记录可靠。

senses.title: The watcher in quantum theory
senses.definition: in quantum mechanics, the agent whose measurement fixes one of the possible outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 在量子力学中，其测量使某个可能结果确定下来的角色
senses.example: In quantum theory the observer cannot be left out of the account.
senses.exampleCN: 在量子理论里，观察者无法被排除在描述之外。
senses.why: If a measurement changes the state it measures, the watcher becomes part of the system, and the word carries that problem.
senses.whyCN: 如果测量改变了被测量的状态，观看者就成了系统的一部分，这个词正承担着这一难题。

senses.title: A seat without a vote
senses.definition: a representative allowed to attend and speak at a body but not to vote
senses.definitionCN: 获准出席并发言、但没有表决权的代表
senses.example: The body granted the agency observer status.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构给了这个组织观察员地位。
senses.why: An organisation that watches but does not decide needs a name between member and guest, and this is it.
senses.whyCN: 只看不决定的组织需要一个介于成员与客人之间的身份，这个词正好补上。

senses.title: The monitor at an election
senses.definition: a person sent to watch that a vote is conducted fairly and to report on it
senses.definitionCN: 被派去监督投票是否公正并提交报告的人
senses.example: An observer from each party stood at every ballot box.
senses.exampleCN: 每个投票箱旁都站着一名各党派的观察员。
senses.why: A watcher with a mandate to report turns looking into a safeguard, so the word gains a public function.
senses.whyCN: 负有报告职责的观看者把「看」变成一种保障，这个词于是有了公共职能。

senses.title: The researcher who joins in
senses.definition: in anthropology, a researcher who lives among the people studied while still recording
senses.definitionCN: 在人类学中与被研究者共同生活、同时坚持记录的研究者
senses.example: The observer joined the factory shift to understand the work.
senses.exampleCN: 这位观察者加入工厂班次，以理解那份工作。
senses.why: Some behaviour only appears to insiders, so the method accepts participation while trying to keep the record honest.
senses.whyCN: 有些行为只对内部人显现，因此这种方法允许参与，同时设法保持记录诚实。

senses.title: The impartial witness
senses.definition: a person present who can report what happened without a stake in the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 在场且与结果无利害关系、能陈述发生了什么的人
senses.example: To a neutral observer the mistake was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 在中立的观察者看来，那个错误一目了然。
senses.why: Someone with no stake can be trusted to say what a participant cannot, and the word supplies that position.
senses.whyCN: 没有利害关系的人能说出参与者说不出口的话，这个词提供了这一位置。

senses.title: The officer at a ceasefire line
senses.definition: a soldier or official deployed to watch a truce or a disputed border and report violations
senses.definitionCN: 被派去监督停火或争议边界、并报告违规行为的军人或官员
senses.example: Military observers reported two breaches before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军事观察员报告黎明前有两起违约。
senses.why: Where two sides will not share a patrol, a third party watches, and the watching is the whole job.
senses.whyCN: 双方不愿共同巡逻时，就由第三方来看，而「看」本身就是全部工作。

senses.title: A perceptive commentator
senses.definition: a person known for noticing and describing what others miss, often in public writing
senses.definitionCN: 以察觉并描述他人忽略之处著称的人，常见于公共写作
senses.example: She is a sharp observer of how committees really decide.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位敏锐的观察者，看得出委员会真正如何决定。
senses.why: Long practice in watching produces someone whose remarks are trusted, and the plain word for watcher becomes praise.
senses.whyCN: 长期观看的练习造就一个其评论可信的人，于是「观看者」这个朴素词成了赞誉。

intro.en: Observer is observe plus the agent ending -er, with Latin observator behind it. The science sense is early modern, and the quantum sense is a twentieth-century extension of it.
intro.cn: observer 是 observe 加施事词尾 -er 构成，背后有拉丁语 observator。科学观测义属近代早期，量子力学义则是二十世纪对它的延伸。

items.en: Observare meant to watch over and heed, from ob- 'over' and servare 'to keep'.
items.cn: observare 意为看守并留心，由 ob-「在……之上」与 servare「保持」构成。

items.en: Late Latin observator named the person who watched or kept a rule, a model for the English agent noun.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 observator 指观看或守规的人，为英语的施事名词提供了样板。

items.en: The English agent ending came from Old English -ere, itself borrowed from Latin -arius, so the two halves meet again.
items.cn: 英语施事词尾来自古英语 -ere，而 -ere 又借自拉丁语 -arius，两半在英语里重新汇合。

items.en: Observer entered English in the sixteenth century, at first for a person who keeps a rule or a custom.
items.cn: observer 在十六世纪进入英语，最初指遵守规则或习俗的人。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy and natural history gave the word its recording sense, with instruments and notebooks.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学与博物学给了它「用仪器与记录本观看」的含义。

items.en: The twentieth century added the observer in quantum measurement and the observer sent to watch elections and ceasefires.
items.cn: 二十世纪又加上量子测量中的观察者，以及被派去监督选举与停火的观察员。

note.en: The first group shares the watching root; the second group names related onlooker roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享「观看」词根；第二组是相关的旁观角色。

entries.definition: The verb of watching, keeping and remarking.
entries.definitionCN: 表示观看、遵守与评论的动词。

entries.definition: The act or the recorded result of watching.
entries.definitionCN: 观看的行为，或被记录下来的结果。

entries.definition: Quick to notice; also careful about rules.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉敏锐的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: A building equipped for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 装备起来观测天空的建筑。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rite or rule, not the person who watches.
entries.definitionCN: 对仪式或规则的遵行，不是观看的人。

entries.definition: Someone who watches an event without taking part; no scientific weight.
entries.definitionCN: 观看事件而不参与的人；没有科研分量。

entries.definition: A person who saw an event and can testify to it.
entries.definitionCN: 看见事件并能作证的人。

entries.definition: A person or device that keeps a continuous check.
entries.definitionCN: 持续进行检查的人或装置。

entries.definition: A member of an audience, there to be entertained.
entries.definitionCN: 观众之一，为观赏而来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin watcher, the real family and the fixed titles of research and missions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语中的观看者、真实同族词，以及科研与派驻任务里的固定头衔。

normal.en: Observer is the verb of watching plus the person ending, and Latin already had a watcher noun.
normal.cn: observer 是观看动词加表示人的词尾，拉丁语里本就有「观看者」这一名词。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Research has a second observer check the timings, so the record can be trusted.
normal.cn: 研究中让第二位观察者核对计时，记录才可信。

normal.en: Elections and ceasefires both send observers, because a report needs a witness.
normal.cn: 选举与停火都派观察员，因为报告需要见证者。

normal.en: The observer effect names the trouble that watching can change what is watched.
normal.cn: 观察者效应命名「观看可能改变被观看之物」这一麻烦。

abstract.en: An observer is paid to be unnoticed, and noticed only in the report.
abstract.cn: 观察者的本分是不被注意，只在报告里被注意。

abstract.en: The best observer knows which detail would change the conclusion.
abstract.cn: 最好的观察者知道哪个细节会改变结论。

abstract.en: Watching without a stake is the quietest kind of power.
abstract.cn: 无利害关系的观看，是最安静的一种权力。

examples.en: Each observer recorded the same session on a separate sheet.
examples.cn: 每位观察者用各自的表格记录同一场活动。

examples.en: The observer noted that the queue moved faster after noon.
examples.cn: 观察者注意到中午之后队伍移动更快。

examples.en: An observer may speak at the meeting but may not vote.
examples.cn: 观察员可以在会上发言，但没有表决权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽弗」——守在旁边只看不插手的那个人：观察者

root: observe（拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」）+ 施事词尾 -er（古英语 -ere，借自拉丁语 -arius）；拉丁语本有 observator。科学义见于十七世纪，量子与政治观察员义为二十世纪延伸。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one silent watcher: the non-participant, the study recorder, the quantum measurer, the seat without a vote, the election monitor, the participant researcher, the impartial witness, the ceasefire officer and the perceptive commentator.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一个沉默的观看者：不参与者、研究记录者、量子测量者、无表决权席位、选举监督者、参与式研究者、公正见证者、停火军官与眼光锐利的评论者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in the last row writes in a notebook and never raises a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一排的人在本子上记录，从不举手。

branches.en: THE ONLOOKER: present without a part, and trusted because there is no stake.
branches.cn: 旁观者：在场而不参与，因无利害而被信任。

branches.en: THE RESEARCH WATCHER: one of two recorders, or a researcher who lives among the studied.
branches.cn: 研究中的观看者：两名记录者之一，或与被研究者共同生活的研究者。

branches.en: THE MEASURER: the watcher whose act of watching enters the system being described.
branches.cn: 测量者：其观看动作进入了被描述系统的观看者。

branches.en: THE MANDATED WATCHER: a seat without a vote, a monitor at a ballot box, an officer on a truce line.
branches.cn: 受命观看者：无表决权的席位、投票箱旁的监督者、停火线上的军官。

branches.en: THE REMARKER: long watching turned into trusted comment.
branches.cn: 评论者：长期观看变成可信的评论。

intro.en: Observer is a Latin verb plus an agent ending that English borrowed twice over, once directly from Latin and once through Old English.
intro.cn: observer 是一个拉丁动词加施事词尾，而这个词尾被英语借了两次，一次直接来自拉丁语，一次经古英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is observare, servare and observator, with -or and -arius as agent endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 observare、servare 与 observator，施事词尾有 -or 与 -arius。

items.example: The person noun is built on the verb, not on a Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个表示人的名词建在动词上，而非拉丁名词上。

items.example: The verb supplies the action the person performs.
items.exampleCN: 动词提供这个人所做的动作。

items.example: It also gives preserve and reserve.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「保存」与「保留」两词的来源。

items.meaning: a watcher; a keeper of rules
items.example: Latin had the person noun before English did.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语先有这个人名词。

items.example: It builds observator, creator and narrator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成观察者、创造者与叙述者。

items.example: English prefers this ending for everyday agents.
items.exampleCN: 英语日常施事名词多用这个词尾。

items.example: It is the older shape behind the English ending.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词尾背后更早的形态。

items.example: The noun names the activity, not the person.
The adjective describes the habit the person has.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述这个人所具有的习惯。

items.example: The place noun extends the family to buildings.
items.exampleCN: 场所名词把词族扩展到建筑。

latinEntries.example: The verb is the direct source of observe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是 observe 的直接来源。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb servare (serv-, servatum; to keep)
latinEntries.example: It supplies the keeping and guarding idea.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它提供「看守、守护」这层意思。
拉丁语 observator 意为观看者。

latinEntries.example: Latin -or builds nouns such as doctor and rector.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -or 构成 doctor、rector 这类名词。

definition_zh: 舒适地；轻松地；宽裕地
definition_en: in a way that gives physical ease, with little difficulty, or with enough money
core_image: 半躺在沙发上，手脚都找到最放松的位置
scene: 老人把椅子放低，靠着垫子安稳地睡着了。 She sat comfortably by the window with a book.
sceneCN: 这里 comfortably 指「舒适地」（第 1 个义项：身体放松自在）；句意是她舒适地坐在窗边看书。

senses.title: In a comfortable way
senses.definition: in a way that gives or shows physical ease
senses.definitionCN: 以身体放松舒服的方式
senses.example: The old dog lay comfortably by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 老狗舒舒服服地躺在火边。
senses.why: The adverb simply describes how the body rests, which is the base sense.
senses.whyCN: 副词只是描述身体如何休息，这正是最基础的义项。

senses.title: With ease
senses.definition: easily and without difficulty, especially in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 毫不费力地，尤指在比赛中
senses.example: The team won comfortably by three goals.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队以三个球的优势轻松获胜。
senses.why: Effortless ease of body becomes effortless ease of action.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的不费力，变成了行动上的不费力。

senses.title: With enough money
senses.definition: with enough money to live well and without worry
senses.definitionCN: 钱够用、生活无忧地
senses.example: They live comfortably on one salary.
senses.exampleCN: 他们靠一份薪水就过得宽裕。
senses.why: A life without pressure is comfortable, so the adverb also covers money.
senses.whyCN: 没有压力的生活就是舒适的，所以这个副词也涵盖钱财。

intro.en: Comfortably is comfortable plus -ly, the usual ending for English adverbs of manner.
intro.cn: comfortably 由 comfortable 加 -ly 构成，这是英语方式副词的常规词尾。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, and confortare meant to strengthen.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮，confortare 意为使增强。

items.en: Old French conforter gave English its comfort.
items.cn: 古法语 conforter 给了英语 comfort 这个词。

items.en: Comfort first named strength and encouragement.
items.cn: comfort 最初指力量与鼓励。

items.en: Comfortable shifted to physical ease, and the adverb followed.
items.cn: comfortable 转向身体的安适，副词形式随之出现。

items.en: Comfortably now also means easily and with money to spare.
items.cn: 如今 comfortably 还表示轻松地、手头宽裕地。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adverbs with the same -ably rhythm, while the meaning group gives other adverbs of ease.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同样带 -ably 节奏的副词，近义组给出其他表示轻松自在的副词。

entries.definition: much; to a large degree
entries.definitionCN: 相当大地；很大程度上

entries.definition: in a way that shows approval
entries.definitionCN: 赞许地；有利地

entries.definition: in a surprising way
entries.definitionCN: 显著地；出奇地

entries.definition: without effort or difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 毫不费力地

entries.definition: in a warm and sheltered way
entries.definitionCN: 温暖舒适地

entries.definition: in a close and warm position
entries.definitionCN: 紧贴而温暖地

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a body settling down, then move to an easy win and to a full purse.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从身体安顿下来开始，再走到轻松的胜利与充足的钱包。

normal.en: The -ly ending marks the adverb, so comfortably tells how something is done.
normal.cn: -ly 结尾标记副词，所以 comfortably 说明事情是怎样做的。

normal.en: Sit comfortably, sleep comfortably, live comfortably: body, night, life.
normal.cn: 坐得舒适、睡得安稳、活得宽裕：身体、夜晚、生活。

normal.en: A team that wins comfortably never needs a last-minute goal.
normal.cn: 轻松取胜的队伍不需要最后一分钟的进球。

normal.en: Comfortably off means there is money left at the end of the month.
normal.cn: 手头宽裕是指月底还有余钱。

normal.en: Drop the -ly and the adjective comfortable appears.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ly，形容词 comfortable 就出现了。

abstract.en: Picture a cat stretched across a sunny windowsill.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫摊开身体躺在向阳的窗台上。

abstract.en: Picture a runner crossing the line well ahead of others.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者远远领先冲过终点线。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet dinner where no bill is being counted.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿安静的晚餐，没人算计账单。

examples.en: She read comfortably in the soft light.
examples.cn: 她在柔和的灯光下舒适地阅读。

examples.en: The home team won comfortably in the end.
examples.cn: 主队最终轻松获胜。

examples.en: His parents are comfortably off these days.
examples.cn: 他父母如今手头宽裕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comfortably 记成 comfortable（舒适的）加 ly：以舒适的方式做事，就是舒适地。

root: 由 comfortable 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，词根可上溯拉丁语 fortis（强壮）与 confortare（使增强），本义是以得力的方式，后转为舒适地。

sensesIntro.en: From the way the body rests, to the way a match is won, and finally to the way money lasts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体休息的方式，到比赛取胜的方式，再到钱够用的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lying half back on a sofa with every limb at rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：半躺在沙发上，手脚都找到最放松的位置。

branches.en: The physical sense is the base for all the others.
branches.cn: 身体上的义项是其余义项的基础。

branches.en: An easy win is comfort applied to effort.
branches.cn: 轻松的胜利是把舒适用在力气上。

branches.en: Money enough for needs is comfort applied to daily life.
branches.cn: 够用的钱是把舒适用在日常生活上。

branches.en: Both a resting body and a winning team show no strain.
branches.cn: 休息的身体与获胜的队伍都看不出紧绷。

branches.en: Ease in a match and ease in a budget feel much alike.
branches.cn: 赛场上的轻松与预算上的轻松感觉很像。

intro.en: Comfortably is an adverb built from an adjective, and the whole family circles around comfort.
intro.cn: comfortably 是由形容词构成的副词，整个家族都围绕 comfort 展开。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem fort- for strong still sits under the endings.
latinIntro.cn: 表示强壮的拉丁词干 fort- 仍藏在层层词尾之下。

items.example: The sofa is wide and comfortable.
He shifted uncomfortably in his seat.
items.exampleCN: 他在座位上不自在地挪动。
这消息莫名地令人宽慰。

items.meaning: a person who comforts or a warm cover
items.exampleCN: 她把厚被子叠得整整齐齐。

items.example: The corridor was bare and comfortless.
items.exampleCN: 走廊光秃秃的，很不舒适。

items.example: Hot water is one of life's comforts.
items.exampleCN: 热水是生活中的一种舒适。

items.example: The tight band caused some discomfort.
items.exampleCN: 过紧的带子带来了一些不适。

definition_zh: 家用电器；器具；装置
definition_en: a machine or device used in the home or workplace for a particular job
core_image: 厨房台面上一排插着电的机器
scene: 搬家那天，纸箱里装的都是电饭锅、熨斗这类东西。 The kitchen is fitted with modern appliances.
sceneCN: 这里 appliance 是「家用电器」（第 1 个义项：家中使用的机器设备）；句意是厨房配了现代化电器。

pos.zh: 名词：家用电器；器具；装置

derivatives.zh: 动词：应用；申请，与 appliance 同根

senses.title: A household machine
senses.definition: an electrical machine used in the home, such as a fridge or a washing machine
senses.definitionCN: 家中使用的电器，如冰箱或洗衣机
senses.example: The kitchen is fitted with modern appliances.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房配了现代化电器。
senses.why: The word comes from apply, 'to put to use', so an appliance is a thing applied to a practical task.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 apply「应用」，所以 appliance 就是被用来完成某项实用任务的物件。

senses.title: A device for a specific job
senses.definition: any apparatus designed for a particular purpose, not only in the home
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的设计的任何器械，不限于家庭
senses.example: Dental appliances must be cleaned daily.
senses.exampleCN: 牙科矫治器必须每天清洁。
senses.why: If the word names anything put to a use, it can cover medical and industrial devices as well as kitchen machines.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词指任何被投入使用的东西，那么它就能涵盖医疗器械与工业装置，而不只是厨房机器。

intro.en: Appliance is built on the verb apply, with the sense 'something applied to a task'.
intro.cn: appliance 建立在动词 apply 之上，意为「被用于某项任务的东西」。

items.en: applicare meant 'to fold to, attach'.
items.cn: applicare 意为「贴上去、附着」。

items.en: aplier gave English the verb apply.
items.cn: aplier 给英语带来了动词 apply。

items.en: Appliance first meant the act of applying.
items.cn: appliance 最初指「应用」这一行为。

items.en: The sense shifted to the thing applied, especially a device.
items.cn: 词义转向被应用的物件，尤指器械。

items.en: In the twentieth century it narrowed mainly to household machines.
items.cn: 二十世纪它主要收窄为家用机器。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the apply root; the near-meaning group gives other words for equipment.
note.cn: 形近组共享 apply 词根；近义组是其他表示设备的词。

entries.definition: to put to use or ask formally
entries.definitionCN: 应用；申请

entries.definition: able to be applied
entries.definitionCN: 适用的

entries.definition: a person who applies
entries.definitionCN: 申请人

entries.definition: a machine made for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 装置

entries.definition: a powered apparatus
entries.definitionCN: 机器

entries.definition: a tool used in a kitchen
entries.definitionCN: 厨房用具

normalIntro.en: An appliance is something you apply to the work of living.
normalIntro.cn: appliance 就是被用在日常生活里的东西。

normal.en: Household appliance is the standard formal phrase.
normal.cn: household appliance 是标准的正式说法。

normal.en: The verb is apply, the noun is appliance.
normal.cn: 动词是 apply，名词是 appliance。

normal.en: Kitchen appliances covers fridge, oven, and dishwasher.
normal.cn: kitchen appliances 包括冰箱、烤箱与洗碗机。

normal.en: Do not confuse appliance with application; the first is a machine.
normal.cn: 不要把 appliance 与 application 混淆，前者是机器。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PPLI-ance.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-PPLI-ance。

abstract.en: See a counter crowded with plugged-in machines.
abstract.cn: 想象插着电、挤满台面的机器。

abstract.en: See a repairman opening a washing machine.
abstract.cn: 想象维修工打开洗衣机。

abstract.en: See a row of switches on a kitchen wall.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房墙上一排开关。

examples.en: The kitchen is fitted with modern appliances.
examples.cn: 厨房配了现代化电器。

examples.en: Dental appliances must be cleaned daily.
examples.cn: 牙科矫治器必须每天清洁。

examples.en: The shop sells household appliances at low prices.
examples.cn: 这家店以低价出售家用电器。

dict_mnemonic.text: apply（应用）加 -ance（名词）：拿来用的东西，器具。

root: 由动词 apply 加名词词尾 -ance 构成；apply 源于拉丁语 applicare「贴上、附着」，因此 appliance 本义是「被应用的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Any device applied to a practical job, from kitchen machines to dental fittings.
sensesIntro.cn: 任何被用于实际任务的装置，从厨房机器到牙科矫治器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a machine switched on to do a job for you.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台开动起来替你干活的机器。

branches.en: kitchen appliances
branches.cn: 厨房电器

branches.en: a household appliance
branches.cn: 家用电器

branches.en: appliance repair
branches.cn: 家电维修

branches.en: a dental appliance
branches.cn: 牙科矫治器

branches.en: an industrial appliance
branches.cn: 工业装置

intro.en: A noun built on apply, one of the most productive Latin verbs in English.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在 apply 之上的名词，而 apply 是英语中构词力最强的拉丁动词之一。

latinIntro.en: The root applicare, 'to attach', underlies the whole apply family.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 applicare「附着」支撑着整个 apply 词族。

items.meaning: a device applied to a task
a thing made for a purpose

definition_zh: 严重地；严肃地；阴郁地
definition_en: in a very serious way
core_image: 医生严肃地摘下眼镜
scene: 医生严肃地说明了病情。 The doctor spoke gravely about the illness.
sceneCN: 这里 gravely 是「严肃地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：医生严肃地说明了病情。

senses.title: To a severe degree
senses.definition: to a very serious or severe degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到非常严重的程度
senses.example: The building was gravely damaged.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑严重受损。
senses.why: Severity is the first sense of the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 严重程度是副词的第一义。

senses.title: Solemnly
senses.definition: in a serious and solemn manner
senses.definitionCN: 以严肃庄重的方式
senses.example: The doctor spoke gravely about the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 医生严肃地说明了病情。
senses.why: The manner sense moves from events to voice.
senses.whyCN: 由事态转向说话的神态。

senses.title: Darkly
senses.definition: in a dark or gloomy way
senses.definitionCN: 以阴沉、忧郁的方式
senses.example: The bells rang gravely at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时钟声沉郁地响起。
senses.why: Sound and atmosphere take on the same weight.
senses.whyCN: 声音与氛围也带上了这种沉重。

intro.en: Gravely is the adverb of grave, from Latin gravis, heavy.
intro.cn: gravely 是 grave 的副词形式，源自拉丁语 gravis（沉重）。

items.en: Gravis meant heavy.
items.cn: gravis 意为沉重的。

items.en: A heavy matter was a serious matter.
items.cn: 沉重之事即严重之事。

items.en: Grave entered English as serious.
items.cn: grave 以「严重的」之义进入英语。

items.en: The adverb gravely added -ly.
items.cn: 副词 gravely 由加 -ly 构成。

items.en: It described both danger and solemn tone.
items.cn: 它既形容危险，也形容庄重的语气。

note.en: Gravely is compared with look-alike words and words for seriousness.
note.cn: 把 gravely 与形近词以及表示严肃的词作比较。

entries.definition: showing courage
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢的

entries.definition: the force of falling
entries.definitionCN: 重力

entries.definition: small stones
entries.definitionCN: 砾石

entries.definition: in a serious way
entries.definitionCN: 严重地；严肃地

entries.definition: in a formal serious way
entries.definitionCN: 庄重地

entries.definition: to a great or severe degree
entries.definitionCN: 严重地

normalIntro.en: Gravely is grave turned into an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: gravely 就是变成副词的 grave。

normal.en: She is gravely ill.
normal.cn: 她病得很重。

normal.en: He shook his head gravely.
normal.cn: 他严肃地摇了摇头。

normal.en: The report is gravely wrong.
normal.cn: 这份报告有严重错误。

normal.en: They spoke gravely of the loss.
normal.cn: 他们沉重地谈到这场损失。

normal.en: The judge looked at him gravely.
normal.cn: 法官严肃地看着他。

abstract.en: Some news must be said slowly and gravely.
abstract.cn: 有些消息，必须缓慢而严肃地说。

abstract.en: Weight in the voice tells the truth first.
abstract.cn: 声音里的重量，最先说出真相。

abstract.en: The gravest words are often the shortest.
abstract.cn: 最沉重的话，往往最短。

examples.en: The building was gravely damaged.
examples.cn: 这栋建筑严重受损。

examples.en: The doctor spoke gravely about the illness.
examples.cn: 医生严肃地说明了病情。

examples.en: The bells rang gravely at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时钟声沉郁地响起。

dict_mnemonic.text: gravely 是 grave 加 -ly 构成的副词，既表示「严重地」，也表示「严肃地」；gravely ill 是病重，speak gravely 是严肃地说。

root: 由 grave（严重的、严肃的）加 -ly 构成，词根源自拉丁语 gravis（沉重），核心义为「以沉重的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Gravely means severely, solemnly, or darkly.
sensesIntro.cn: gravely 指严重地、严肃地，或阴郁地。

core.en: Carrying weight into action and voice.
core.cn: 把重量带进行动与声音。

branches.en: A cracked wall leans outward.
branches.cn: 开裂的墙向外倾斜。

branches.en: A doctor folds her hands before speaking.
branches.cn: 医生说话前交叠双手。

branches.en: Bells move slowly through evening air.
branches.cn: 钟声在暮色中缓缓移动。

branches.en: Severity shows in facts and in faces.
branches.cn: 严重既显于事，也显于脸。

branches.en: A solemn voice and a dark bell are kin.
branches.cn: 庄重的声音与沉郁的钟，是近亲。

intro.en: Gravely belongs to a family built on grave and gravity.
intro.cn: gravely 属于由 grave 与 gravity 构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gravis, heavy.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 gravis，意为沉重。

items.example: The graveness of the case was clear.
He felt the gravity of the moment.

definition_zh: 发育的；发展的；成长阶段的
definition_en: relating to the growth and change of a person, thing or system
core_image: 墙上一条条铅笔线，每道线旁写着量身高的日期
scene: 诊所的墙上画着一道道铅笔线，每道线旁都写着日期。 The doctor checked the child's developmental milestones.
sceneCN: 这里 developmental 指「发育的」（第 1 个义项：与身体或心智的成长有关）；句意是医生检查了孩子的发育里程碑。

pos.zh: 发育的；发展的；成长阶段的

senses.title: Relating to physical growth
senses.definition: connected with the way a body or mind grows and matures
senses.definitionCN: 与身体或心智的成长成熟有关的
senses.example: The doctor checked the child's developmental milestones.
senses.exampleCN: 医生检查了孩子的发育里程碑。
senses.why: A growing body keeps a calendar written in inches.
senses.whyCN: 成长中的身体，藏着一本用身高写成的日历。

senses.title: Relating to social change
senses.definition: connected with the growth of an economy, a system or a society
senses.definitionCN: 与经济、制度或社会的成长有关的
senses.example: The report examines developmental policy in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告考察农村地区的发展政策。
senses.why: A whole region can be measured the way a child is.
senses.whyCN: 一整个地区，也能像孩子那样被量出成长。

senses.title: Belonging to an early stage
senses.definition: describing a stage in which something is still forming
senses.definitionCN: 形容某事物仍在成形之中的阶段
senses.example: The plan is still at a developmental stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划仍处在成长阶段。
senses.why: Before it is finished, a thing is only a sketch of itself.
senses.whyCN: 在完成之前，一个东西只是它自己的一张草图。

intro.en: Developmental is development plus -al, and development goes back through French to a word meaning to unwrap.
intro.cn: developmental 是 development 加 -al，而 development 经法语可追到一个意为「打开包裹」的词。

items.en: Developper meant to unwrap or unfold something closed.
items.cn: developper 指把合着的东西打开、展开。

items.en: Development first named the unfolding of a plan or a living thing.
items.cn: development 最初指计划或生物一步一步展开。

items.en: The suffix -al turned the noun into an adjective.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 把这个名词变成了形容词。

items.en: Psychology gave the word a central place in describing stages of growth.
items.cn: 心理学让这个词在描述成长阶段时占据中心位置。

items.en: It now covers biology, education and economic policy alike.
items.cn: 如今它同时覆盖生物学、教育与经济政策。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the develop family, while the meaning group describes things that are still forming.
note.cn: 形近组同属 develop 这一族，近义组则形容仍在成形的事物。

entries.definition: the process of growing or building
entries.definitionCN: 成长或建设的过程

entries.definition: having reached an advanced stage
entries.definitionCN: 已达到较高阶段的

entries.definition: still growing or improving
entries.definitionCN: 仍在成长或改善的

entries.definition: having a strong effect on how something grows
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的成长有强烈影响的

entries.definition: relating to slow natural change
entries.definitionCN: 与缓慢的自然变化有关的

entries.definition: increasing in size or amount
entries.definitionCN: 体积或数量在增加的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with pencil marks on a clinic wall and end with a plan that is still a sketch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从诊所墙上的铅笔线开始，落到一份还是草图的计划。

normal.en: Development plus -al gives you the adjective for anything still unfolding.
normal.cn: development 加上 -al，就是形容「仍在展开」的形容词。

normal.en: A child and an economy both have stages, and both keep records.
normal.cn: 孩子与经济都有阶段，也都留着记录。

normal.en: A milestone is a date written on a wall.
normal.cn: 里程碑就是写在墙上的一道日期。

normal.en: What is developmental is not yet finished, and that is the point.
normal.cn: 说某物处在成长阶段，就是它还没完成，而这正是关键。

normal.en: The pencil line rises slowly; nobody watches it rise.
normal.cn: 铅笔线慢慢升高，没人一直盯着它升。

abstract.en: Picture a door frame marked with small horizontal lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门框上刻着一道道短横线。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook where each year takes one page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记本，每年占一页。

abstract.en: Picture a clay figure still soft in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一个中间还软着的泥人。

examples.en: The doctor checked the child's developmental milestones.
examples.cn: 医生检查了孩子的发育里程碑。

examples.en: The report examines developmental policy in rural areas.
examples.cn: 这份报告考察农村地区的发展政策。

examples.en: The plan is still at a developmental stage.
examples.cn: 这个计划仍处在成长阶段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 developmental 记成「地维勒普门头」：develop 是展开，-ment 是过程，-al 是形容词尾巴，合起来就是与成长过程有关的。

root: 由 develop 加 -ment 构成名词 development，再加形容词后缀 -al 而成。词根可追到法语 developper（打开包裹），本义是展开。十九世纪起用于描述生物个体的发育，二十世纪又扩展到心理学、教育与社会发展。

sensesIntro.en: From a body keeping its own growth calendar, to a region changing, to a plan that is still soft.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体记着自己的成长日历，到一个地区在改变，再到一份还软着的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small pencil marks climbing a wall year after year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道道铅笔线年复一年地往墙上爬。

branches.en: The first sense is the body writing those marks.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是身体写下那些线。

branches.en: The second sense is a whole society making the same climb.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一整个社会在爬同样的坡。

branches.en: The third sense is the soft middle before the shape is fixed.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是形状固定之前那段软软的中间期。

branches.en: A child and a region are both read by their stages.
branches.cn: 孩子与地区，都靠各自的阶段被读懂。

branches.en: Policy and a sketch both belong to the unfinished side.
branches.cn: 政策与草图，都属于尚未完成的那一边。

intro.en: Developmental sits at the adjective end of a family built on growth.
intro.cn: developmental 站在这一族词里形容词的那一端，这族词都建在成长上。

latinIntro.en: The stem means to unwrap, and -ment plus -al turn that action into a quality.
latinIntro.cn: 词干意为打开包裹，-ment 与 -al 把这个动作变成一个性质。

items.exampleCN: 这是一个发育方面的问题。
这个孩子在发育上已经准备好。
开发者资助了这项研究。
这是一个发展中的领域。
这些技能仍未发展起来。

definition_zh: 侄女；外甥女；姻亲的侄女
definition_en: the daughter of one's brother or sister, or of one's spouse's brother or sister
core_image: 饭桌边一个女孩被长辈塞了红包，笑着往口袋里收
scene: 过年时，长辈把红包塞给桌边那个女孩，她低头笑着收进兜里。 My niece stayed by the table until the sweets were gone.
sceneCN: 这里 niece 是「侄女」（第 1 个义项：兄弟姐妹的女儿）；句意为我的侄女一直守在桌边，直到糖都吃完了。图中可辨识物件：饭桌、红包、糖盘。

derivatives.zh: 与 niece 成对，同出拉丁语 nepos 一系，义为「侄子；外甥」
由 great 与 niece 复合而成，义为「侄孙女；甥孙女」
由拉丁语 nepos（后代）加 -ism 构成，义为「任人唯亲」

senses.title: The daughter of one's brother or sister
senses.definition: the female child of one's own brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 自己兄弟或姐妹的女儿
senses.example: My niece stayed by the table until the sweets were gone.
senses.exampleCN: 我的侄女一直守在桌边，直到糖都吃完了。
senses.why: Latin neptis named exactly this corner of the family, a sibling's daughter, and English kept the narrow sense instead of letting the word mean any young girl.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 neptis 指的正是家谱上这一格：兄弟姐妹的女儿；英语保留了这个窄义，没有让它变成「任何小女孩」的通称。

senses.title: The daughter of one's spouse's sibling
senses.definition: the female child of a husband's or wife's brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫或妻子的兄弟、姐妹的女儿
senses.example: His niece by marriage came to the wedding with her own children.
senses.exampleCN: 他妻子那边的侄女带着自己的孩子来参加婚礼。
senses.why: Marriage stretches the same relation sideways, and because English marks the tie rather than the blood, the daughter of a spouse's sibling enters the family under the same word.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻把同一种关系横向拉开；英语标记的是亲属关系而不是血缘，所以配偶兄弟姐妹的女儿也用同一个词进到家里来。

senses.title: A young female relative raised in one's household
senses.definition: a young female relative who lives under one's care, as in older family letters
senses.definitionCN: 旧时家信中指由自己照养的年轻女性亲属
senses.example: The letters call her his niece, though she was the orphan he brought up.
senses.exampleCN: 信里称她为他的侄女，虽然她其实是他抚养长大的孤儿。
senses.why: Households once took in orphaned or poor young relatives, and the word followed the girl into the house, so a guardian could write of his ward as his niece.
senses.whyCN: 旧时家庭会收留失去父母或家境困难的年轻亲属，这个词就跟着女孩进了家门，于是监护人也能把自己的被监护人写作侄女。

intro.en: Niece came to English from Latin by way of French, and it has stayed a narrow label for one branch of the family tree.
intro.cn: niece 由拉丁语经法语进入英语，一直只做家谱某一支的窄标签。

items.en: Neptis meant a brother's or sister's daughter, and it could also stretch to a granddaughter.
items.cn: neptis 指兄弟姐妹的女儿，也可以延伸到孙女。

items.en: The related noun nepos meant a grandson or a descendant, and it is the root behind the later word for favouring one's relatives.
items.cn: 与之相关的名词 nepos 指孙子或后代，它正是后来表示「偏袒亲属」那个词的源头。

items.en: Old French kept the family sense in the form niece and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语以 niece 这一形式保留了这层亲属含义，并在诺曼时期之后传给英语。

items.en: Middle English used niece for a sibling's daughter, while cousin still covered a much wider range of kin.
items.cn: 中古英语用 niece 指兄弟姐妹的女儿，而 cousin 那时还覆盖着范围大得多的亲属。

items.en: Modern English pairs niece with nephew for the two children of a sibling and adds the in-law relation without changing the word.
items.cn: 现代英语把 niece 与 nephew 配成一对，分别指兄弟姐妹的两个孩子，并在不改词形的情况下加上姻亲那一层。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the matching kinship word and two words that only share the spelling; the near-meaning group collects other labels on the family tree.
note.cn: 形近组收与之配对的亲属词，以及只是拼写相近的两个词；近义组收家谱上的其他称谓。

entries.definition: The son of one's brother or sister, the matching word for a boy.
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟姐妹的儿子，与 niece 配对的男性称谓。

entries.definition: Pleasant or agreeable; it only looks close to niece and its Latin root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；只是与 niece 拼写相近，拉丁词根不同。

entries.definition: A shallow recess in a wall, or a suitable role for a person; the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 墙上浅浅的凹处，或某人合适的位置；词根与 niece 不同。

entries.definition: The child of one's aunt or uncle, a wider kinship label than niece.
entries.definitionCN: 姑舅姨伯的孩子，比 niece 覆盖面更宽的亲属称谓。

entries.definition: The sister of one's parent, or the wife of one's uncle.
entries.definitionCN: 父母的姐妹，或叔伯舅的妻。

entries.definition: A person connected to another by blood or marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与某人相连的人；亲属。

normalIntro.en: The word is a narrow Latin label for a sibling's daughter that French carried into English, and its small family includes nephew and nepotism.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中给「兄弟姐妹的女儿」的窄标签，经法语带入英语；它的小词族还包括 nephew 与 nepotism。

normal.en: Latin neptis named a sibling's daughter and sometimes a granddaughter, so the word never meant any girl, only a related one.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 neptis 指兄弟姐妹的女儿，有时也指孙女，所以这个词从不指随便哪个女孩，只指有亲缘的那一个。

normal.en: Nephew is the matching word for a boy, and the pair comes from the same Latin family of kinship terms.
normal.cn: nephew 是配对的男性词，这一对都出自拉丁语同一族亲属称谓。

normal.en: The final e is silent, so niece rhymes with peace and not with nice.
normal.cn: 词尾的 e 不发音，所以 niece 与 peace 押韵，而不是与 nice。

normal.en: Great-niece adds one generation, being the daughter of a niece or a nephew.
normal.cn: great-niece 多出一代，指侄女或侄子的女儿。

normal.en: Nepotism comes from the same Latin root for descendant, which shows how far a family word can travel.
normal.cn: nepotism 出自同一个表示「后代」的拉丁词根，可见一个亲属词能走多远。

abstract.en: A word kept for one exact corner of the family tree shows how carefully English labels kinship.
abstract.cn: 一个只守在家谱某一格的词，说明英语给亲属关系贴标签有多仔细。

abstract.en: Because niece marks the relation and not the blood, marriage can hand the title to a new person without changing the word.
abstract.cn: 因为 niece 标记的是关系而非血缘，婚姻能把这一称谓交给新的人，而词本身毫无变化。

abstract.en: The silent e and the long vowel make niece sound like peace, a small accident that memory can put to use.
abstract.cn: 不发音的 e 与长元音让 niece 听起来像 peace，这个小巧合正好可以拿来记。

examples.en: My niece stayed by the table until the sweets were gone.
examples.cn: 我的侄女一直守在桌边，直到糖都吃完了。

examples.en: He drove his niece to school every morning that winter.
examples.cn: 那个冬天他每天早上送侄女上学。

examples.en: She is not my daughter but my niece, the child of my younger sister.
examples.cn: 她不是我女儿，是我的外甥女，我妹妹的孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妮子」——家里那个小妮子就是侄女；记住 niece 是侄女。

root: 拉丁语 neptis（兄弟姐妹的女儿，也可指孙女）经古法语 niece 进入英语；与 nephew 同出一系，nepotism 亦源自拉丁语 nepos（后代）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a sibling's daughter; the second sense reaches the same relation by marriage, and the third follows a young relative into the household.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是兄弟姐妹的女儿；第二个义项由婚姻抵达同一层关系，第三个义项则跟着一个年轻亲属进了家门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a girl at the family table, a red envelope pressed into her hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：饭桌边一个女孩，手里被塞进一个红包。

branches.en: a red envelope handed across the table
branches.cn: 从桌子对面递过来的红包

branches.en: a school gate where an uncle waits each morning
branches.cn: 叔叔每天早上等候的校门口

branches.en: a wedding guest introduced as a niece by marriage
branches.cn: 婚礼上被介绍为姻亲侄女的客人

branches.en: an orphan girl written into a family letter
branches.cn: 被写进家书的孤女

branches.en: two girls calling the same woman aunt
branches.cn: 两个女孩都叫同一个女人姑姑

intro.en: The word rests on a single Latin kinship noun and its close relative, and English built the matching male term and a word about favouring kin on the same base.
intro.cn: 这个词立在一个拉丁语亲属名词及其近亲上，英语又在同一基础上造出配对的男性称谓和表示偏袒亲属的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin neptis is the direct source, and nepos, its close relative, stands behind the English words about descendants and family favour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neptis 是直接来源，它的近亲 nepos 则是英语中表示后代与偏袒亲属那些词的底子。

definition_zh: 肥沃的；富饶的；多产的；能生育的
definition_en: of soil, able to produce good crops, of a mind, producing many ideas, or able to have young

scene: 犁一过，黑油油的泥土翻起来，湿润而松软。 The river valley has fertile soil.

senses.title: Rich soil
senses.definition: of land, able to produce many healthy plants
senses.definitionCN: 土地能长出许多健壮植物
senses.example: The river valley has fertile soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河谷拥有肥沃的土壤。
senses.why: This is the basic agricultural sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的农业义。

senses.title: Rich and productive
senses.definition: producing a large amount of something valuable
senses.definitionCN: 出产大量有价值的东西
senses.example: Trade made the region fertile and wealthy.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易让这个地区富饶起来。
senses.why: Land that bears much is called fertile.
senses.whyCN: 出产丰厚的地方也被称作 fertile。

senses.title: Full of ideas
senses.definition: of a mind, producing many ideas
senses.definitionCN: 头脑能产生许多想法
senses.example: She has a fertile imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 她有丰富的想象力。
senses.why: The image of rich soil extends to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 肥沃土壤的意象延伸到头脑。

senses.title: Able to reproduce
senses.definition: able to have young or produce seeds
senses.definitionCN: 能够生育后代或产生种子
senses.example: The eggs remained fertile for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这些卵在一周内仍能受精发育。
senses.why: Biology uses fertile for the power to reproduce.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用 fertile 表示繁殖能力。

items.en: Ferre meant to bear or carry.
items.cn: ferre 意为承载、出产。

items.en: Fertilis meant able to bear fruit.
items.cn: fertilis 意为能结果实的。

items.en: Fertile passed into French with the same sense.

items.en: English fertile described rich land.

items.en: The word spread to minds and to biology.

note.en: Fertile is compared with similar-looking words and with words for productivity.

entries.definition: to make soil richer or an egg able to grow

entries.definition: producing a lot of something good

entries.definitionCN: 多产的

normalIntro.en: Fertile means able to produce life or ideas in abundance.
normalIntro.cn: fertile 意为能大量出产生命或想法。

normal.en: Fertile comes from a verb meaning to bear.
normal.cn: fertile 出自一个意为「承载、出产」的动词。

normal.en: A fertile mind invents many ideas.

abstract.en: Fertility is the power to turn one thing into many.
abstract.cn: 丰产，是把一变成多的力量。

abstract.en: A fertile idea feeds other ideas.
abstract.cn: 一个有生命力的想法会滋养别的想法。

abstract.en: Even rich ground needs rest.
abstract.cn: 再肥沃的土地也需要休养。

examples.en: The river valley has fertile soil.

examples.en: She has a fertile imagination.

branches.en: Soil that gives strong plants.
