core_image: 一块系在绳端的铅锤从船舷边笔直坠入深水
scene: 船舷边的水手松开手里的绳子，铅锤带着水花沉了下去。 The temperature plunged below zero before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 plunge 是「猛降」（第 1 个义项：突然而急剧地下落）；句意为天亮前气温骤降到零度以下。图中可辨识物件：船舷、绳索、铅锤、水花。

derivatives.zh: 由 plunge 加 -er 构成，义为「活塞；跳水者；鲁莽的人」
由 plunge 加 -ing 构成，义为「骤降的；开得很低的（领口）」
与 plunge 同出拉丁语 plumbum（铅），义为「垂直坠落；骤降」

senses.title: A sudden steep fall
senses.definition: to fall or drop suddenly and by a large amount, especially of prices, temperatures or values
senses.definitionCN: 突然且大幅度地下落，尤指价格、气温或数值
senses.example: The temperature plunged below zero before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前气温骤降到零度以下。
senses.why: The oldest image behind the word is a lead weight dropping straight down; because lead falls fast and without hesitation, the word took on the sense of a sharp fall in number, price or temperature.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后最古老的画面是一块铅锤笔直落下；铅落得又快又毫不犹豫，于是这个词有了数值、价格或气温急剧下跌的意思。

senses.title: To jump or dive into water
senses.definition: to jump or dive quickly into deep water, usually so that the body goes under the surface
senses.definitionCN: 迅速跳入或扎入深水，身体通常没入水面之下
senses.example: She plunged into the cold lake and swam toward the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 她一头扎进冰冷的湖水，朝小船游去。
senses.why: A lead weight sinks at once, and a diver who enters the water the same way is said to plunge; the verb keeps the idea of a body committing itself to the depth without slowing down.
senses.whyCN: 铅锤一入水就下沉，以同样方式入水的潜水者也就叫 plunge；这个动词保留着身体毫不迟疑地交给深处的那层意思。

senses.title: To throw oneself into an activity
senses.definition: to begin an activity or enter a situation with sudden energy, or to put someone into a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 带着突然的劲头开始某项活动或进入某种处境，也指使某人陷入困境
senses.example: He plunged into the new job without reading the brief.
senses.exampleCN: 他没看任务说明就一头扎进新工作里。
senses.why: If a body can plunge into water, it can plunge into work, debt or darkness: the same downward motion describes entering a state so quickly that there is no time to prepare.
senses.whyCN: 身体能扎进水里，也就能扎进工作、债务或黑暗：同样的向下动作，形容进入某种状态快到来不及准备。

senses.title: To push or move with force
senses.definition: to move forward suddenly and with force, or to push something quickly and deeply into something else
senses.definitionCN: 突然用力向前移动，或把某物迅速而深深地插入另一物
senses.example: He plunged the knife into the frozen ground.
senses.exampleCN: 他把刀猛地插进冻硬的地里。
senses.why: The noun sense of a dive gave the verb a second physical use: a hand that drives a blade downward repeats the plunge of the lead, except that a tool now falls instead of a body.
senses.whyCN: 名词「跳水」又给了动词第二个具体用法：手把刀向下送，重复的正是铅锤的下坠，只不过这次落下的是工具而不是身体。

intro.en: Plunge goes back to Latin plumbum, lead: a sounding lead was heaved into the sea to measure depth, and the verb for that act became the verb for diving and for falling fast.
intro.cn: plunge 上溯到拉丁语 plumbum（铅）：人们把测深铅锤抛入海中测量深度，描述这个动作的动词后来变成表示跳水和急速下落的动词。

items.en: Plumbum was the Latin name of lead, the heavy metal used for weights and for sounding the depth of water.
items.cn: plumbum 是拉丁语里「铅」的名称，这种重金属用来做秤锤，也用来测水深。

items.en: The reconstructed verb plumbicare meant to sink like lead or to heave the sounding lead into the sea.
items.cn: 重构的动词 plumbicare 意为像铅一样下沉，或把测深铅锤抛入海中。

items.en: Old French plungier meant to dive, to sink, or to thrust something under water.
items.cn: 古法语 plungier 意为潜水、下沉，或把东西按入水中。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word as plungen, and it covered diving, sinking and pushing a thing deep into another.
items.cn: 中古英语借作 plungen，兼指跳水、下沉以及把东西深深插入另一物。

items.en: Modern English extends the fall from bodies and objects to prices, temperatures and moods, and uses plunge as a noun for a dive or a sharp drop.
items.cn: 现代英语把这种下落从身体与物体扩展到价格、气温与情绪，并用 plunge 作名词表示跳水或骤降。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for lead, which supplies plumb and plummet as well as this verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of going down fast.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语中表示「铅」的词展开，这个词既给出 plumb 与 plummet，也给出这个动词；近义组收表示快速下落的动词。

entries.definition: A piston that pushes down, or a person who dives in boldly.
entries.definitionCN: 向下压的活塞，或贸然行事的人。

entries.definition: To fall straight down very fast; it comes from the same lead weight.
entries.definitionCN: 笔直快速坠落；来自同一个铅锤。

entries.definition: To measure depth, or to test whether a wall is vertical with a lead weight.
entries.definitionCN: 测量深度，或用铅锤检验墙面是否垂直。

entries.definition: Falling steeply, or cut very low at the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 急剧下降的，或领口开得很低的。

entries.definition: To jump head first into water.
entries.definitionCN: 头朝下跳入水中。

entries.definition: To fall or let something fall.
entries.definitionCN: 落下，或让某物落下。

entries.definition: To fall in value or to sit down heavily.
entries.definitionCN: 价值下跌，或重重地坐下。

entries.definition: To go down briefly, or to put something into liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 短暂下降，或把某物浸入液体。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin name of lead, and the family keeps the picture of a heavy weight pulling a line straight down.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「铅」的名称上，词族始终带着「重物把绳子笔直往下拽」的画面。

normal.en: Latin plumbum means lead, so to plunge is literally to go down the way a lead weight goes down.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 plumbum 意为铅，所以 plunge 字面上就是像铅锤那样往下落。

normal.en: Plummet and plumb come from the same metal, which is why all three words suggest a vertical drop or a measured depth.
normal.cn: plummet 与 plumb 都来自同一种金属，所以这三个词都让人想到垂直下落或测量深度。

normal.en: Plunge into work keeps the water image: a person enters the task as a diver enters the sea, all at once.
normal.cn: plunge into work 保留了水的意象：人像潜水者入海那样，一下子进入任务。

normal.en: Take the plunge means to stop hesitating and jump, usually into a commitment such as marriage or a new job.
normal.cn: take the plunge 意为不再犹豫、纵身一跳，通常指结婚或换工作这类承诺。

normal.en: The noun has the same shape as the verb, so a plunge can be either the dive or the fall that follows it.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 a plunge 既可以指那一跳，也可以指随之而来的下跌。

abstract.en: A plunge is a decision made by gravity on someone's behalf.
abstract.cn: 下坠是重力替人做出的决定。

abstract.en: The same motion serves a diver, a share price and a person starting a new life, because all three give up the surface at once.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作适用于跳水者、股价和开始新生活的人，因为三者都是立刻离开表面。

abstract.en: To measure depth with lead is to trust a weight to tell you how far down the bottom is.
abstract.cn: 用铅测深，就是相信一块重物能告诉你底有多深。

examples.en: The temperature plunged below zero before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前气温骤降到零度以下。

examples.en: She plunged into the cold lake and swam toward the boat.
examples.cn: 她一头扎进冰冷的湖水，朝小船游去。

examples.en: He plunged the knife into the frozen ground.
examples.cn: 他把刀猛地插进冻硬的地里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑通」——铅锤扑通一声沉到底；记住 plunge 是猛降，也是跳入。

root: 拉丁语 plumbum（铅）→ 俗拉丁语 plumbicare（抛测深铅）→ 古法语 plungier（潜水、下沉）→ 中古英语 plungen；同族词 plummet、plumb 都含有「铅」这一词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a lead weight dropping straight down; the senses run from measuring depth, to diving under water, to falling sharply in value, to entering a task or a trap all at once.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块铅锤笔直落下；义项从测水深，走到潜入水中，再到数值急剧下跌，最后落到一下子进入某项任务或某个困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lead weight on a line dropping from a ship's side into deep water.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在绳上的铅锤从船舷边坠入深水。

branches.en: a line of mercury dropping in a thermometer
branches.cn: 温度计里汞柱直线下落

branches.en: a diver entering cold water
branches.cn: 跳水者入水

branches.en: a worker buried in a new task
branches.cn: 埋头于新任务的人

branches.en: a blade driven into hard ground
branches.cn: 刀插进硬地

branches.en: share prices falling down a screen
branches.cn: 屏幕上一路下跌的股价

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin noun for lead, a verb meaning to heave the lead, and the French verb that carried the diving sense into English.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「铅」的名词、表示抛铅的动词，以及把跳水义带进英语的法语动词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded behind this word: the noun plumbum, lead, the reconstructed verb plumbicare, to heave the sounding lead, and plumbarius, a worker in lead.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有可考的拉丁形式：名词 plumbum（铅）、重构的动词 plumbicare（抛测深铅），以及 plumbarius（铅匠）。

items.meaning: to dive or to fall sharply

definition_zh: 变量；可变因素；可变物；形容词：可变的、多变的、不稳定的
definition_en: something that can change, or likely to change
core_image: 温度计里的液柱一天里上上下下，数字始终不肯稳住
scene: 实验台上摊着记录表，同一组数据每隔一小时就微微变动一次。 Weather is the hardest variable to control in an outdoor experiment.
sceneCN: 这里 variable 是「变量、可变因素」（第 1 个义项：会变的东西）；句意为天气是户外实验中最难控制的可变因素。液柱上下不定的样子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：变量；可变因素；可变物
形容词：可变的、多变的；不稳定的

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「变化、不同」，是本词的动词形式
名词，义为「可变性、变化幅度」
副词，义为「多变地、不定地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不变的、恒定的」
形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同根

senses.title: A quantity that changes
senses.titleCN: 变量：数学里可取的数值会变
senses.definition: a letter or symbol that can take different numerical values
senses.definitionCN: 可以取不同数值的字母或符号
senses.example: In the equation, x is the variable and two is the constant.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，x 是变量，二则是常数。
senses.why: Latin variare means to change; a variable is simply the name for something allowed to change.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为变化；变量就是「允许变化之物」的名字。

senses.title: A factor in an experiment
senses.titleCN: 实验因素：会影响结果的一项条件
senses.definition: a condition or factor that can differ and so affect a result
senses.definitionCN: 会变化并因此影响结果的条件或因素
senses.example: Weather is the hardest variable to control in an outdoor experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 天气是户外实验中最难控制的可变因素。
senses.why: Science isolates one changing factor at a time, and the word names that chosen factor.
senses.whyCN: 科学一次只隔离一个变化因素，这个词就指那个被选出的因素。

senses.title: Something able to change
senses.titleCN: 可变的东西：性质本身会变动
senses.definition: a thing or quality that is capable of changing
senses.definitionCN: 本身具有变化能力的事物或性质
senses.example: Rainfall in this valley is highly variable from year to year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的降雨量逐年变化很大。
senses.why: The noun and the adjective share one idea: capacity for change, not a fixed state.
senses.whyCN: 名词与形容词共有一个想法：具备变化的能力，而非固定状态。

senses.title: Changeable in character
senses.titleCN: 多变的：形容性格或天气靠不住
senses.definition: likely to change suddenly, used of weather, mood or moody people
senses.definitionCN: 容易突然改变，用于天气、情绪或反复无常的人
senses.example: She has a variable temper, sunny one hour and cold the next.
senses.exampleCN: 她脾气多变，一小时和颜悦色，下一小时就冷若冰霜。
senses.why: The abstract capacity for change becomes a judgement about reliability.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的变化能力，变成了对可靠性的判断。

senses.title: Not constant in cost
senses.titleCN: 可变的成本：随业务量上下浮动
senses.definition: changing with the level of activity, said of costs or prices
senses.definitionCN: 随活动量上下浮动，用于成本或价格
senses.example: Fuel is a variable cost that rises with every extra delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 燃油是一项可变成本，每多送一趟就上涨。
senses.why: Business reuses the mathematical idea: some numbers follow output instead of staying put.
senses.whyCN: 商业沿用了数学的想法：有些数字随产量走，而不是原地不动。

intro.en: Variable comes from Latin variare, to change, through the adjective variabilis and Old French.
intro.cn: variable 来自拉丁语动词 variare「变化」，经形容词 variabilis 与古法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective varius described things spotted, mixed or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述斑驳的、混杂的或多种多样的事物。

items.en: From it came the verb variare, to make different or to alter.
items.cn: 由它派生动词 variare，意为使不同、改变。

items.en: The adjective variabilis meant able to change, built with the suffix -bilis meaning capable.
items.cn: 形容词 variabilis 意为「能变化的」，由后缀 -bilis「能……的」构成。

items.en: Old French passed the word on with the same sense of being changeable.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词传下来，仍保留「会变的」意思。

items.en: In modern mathematics variable became a noun naming the symbol allowed to change.
items.cn: 在现代数学里，variable 变成名词，指允许变化的那个符号。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the vari- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for change and for what is fixed.
note.cn: 形近组沿 vari- 词干；近义组收表示变化以及固定不变的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, to change or differ.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」，是本词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Of several different kinds; the adjective of variety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，属 variety 一支。

entries.definition: A range of different kinds of the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、品种」。

entries.definition: A change or difference in amount or form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化、变异」。

entries.definition: Able to change, plainer and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易变的」，更通俗不带术语味。

entries.definition: Likely to shift or fall; carries a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不稳定的」，带警示意味。

entries.definition: Staying the same; the natural opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「恒定的、常数」，天然的反义词。

entries.definition: Something that affects a result, whether it changes or not.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「因素」，不论变与不变。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the vari- root and real pairs such as variable cost and independent variable.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用 vari- 词根以及 variable cost、independent variable 这样的真实搭配。

normal.en: Vary is the verb, variable is the thing that can vary.
normal.cn: vary 是动词，variable 是那个会变的东西。

normal.en: In maths the variable is the letter, the constant is the number.
normal.cn: 数学里变量是字母，常数是数字。

normal.en: An independent variable is the one you change on purpose.
normal.cn: independent variable 是你故意去改的那个量。

normal.en: Variable costs rise and fall with how much you produce.
normal.cn: variable cost 随产量上下浮动。

normal.en: Add in- and invariable means the opposite: never changing.
normal.cn: 加上 in-，invariable 就是反面：从不改变。

abstract.en: A variable is a slot rather than a value: the name stays, the content keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 变量是一个槽位而不是一个数值：名字不动，内容一直换。

abstract.en: To call something variable is to say its future cannot be read off its present.
abstract.cn: 说某物「可变」，等于说它的未来无法从现状读出。

abstract.en: Every experiment is a bargain: hold most things still so that one thing may move.
abstract.cn: 每个实验都是一笔交易：让大多数东西不动，好让一样东西动起来。

examples.en: Researchers recorded each variable twice a day.
examples.cn: 研究人员每天记录每个变量两次。

examples.en: The results were affected by several variables beyond our control.
examples.cn: 结果受到了几个我们无法控制的可变因素影响。

examples.en: The quality of the soil is highly variable across the farm.
examples.cn: 这片农田的土质差异很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞额波」——威（风）瑞（气）额波一波波变来变去：变量

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 varius「斑驳的、多样的」及其动词 variare「改变」，经 variabilis 与古法语 variable 进入英语；同族词有 vary、various、variety、variation。

sensesIntro.en: Variable moves from a symbol in an equation, to a factor in a lab, to weather, temper and costs.
sensesIntro.cn: variable 从方程里的符号，走到实验室的因素，再到天气、脾气与成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of liquid in a thermometer that will not stay at one mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计里的液柱不肯停在同一刻度上。

branches.en: MATHS LINE: the letter that may take any value.
branches.cn: 数学线：可以取任何值的字母。

branches.en: LAB LINE: the factor you watch or control.
branches.cn: 实验线：你观察或控制的因素。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: rainfall and tempers that shift.
branches.cn: 性质线：会变的雨量和脾气。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: costs that follow output.
branches.cn: 金钱线：随产量走的成本。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variable is the slot, constant is the fixed number.
branches.cn: 对照线：variable 是槽位，constant 是固定数。

intro.en: Variable is the Latin root vari- plus a suffix meaning capable, then an English-looking vowel.
intro.cn: variable 是拉丁词根 vari- 加上表示「能……的」后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is varius, variare and variabilis; all three are attested forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁链条是 varius、variare、variabilis，三者都是可考的实有形式。

definition_zh: 省；行政区；领域；本分；外省
definition_en: a large administrative region of a country, or the area of activity and responsibility that belongs to someone
core_image: 一张地图被笔直的边界线切成几大块，每一块都有自己的名字和衙署
scene: 办公室的墙上挂着一张全国地图，有人用手指沿着边界线划出一大块，又在旁边写下自己的职责范围。 The new railway will run through three provinces in the north.
sceneCN: 这里取「省、行政区」的意思（第 1 个义项：国家划分出的大行政区）；句意为这条新铁路将穿过北方的三个省。地图上被边界线划出的那一大块就是线索。

pos.zh: 省；行政区；领域；本分；外省

collocations.zh: 在首都以外的地方；在地方上

derivatives.zh: 由 province 加 -ial 构成，义为「省的；地方的；眼界狭隘的」
由 provincial 加 -ism 构成，义为「地方观念；偏狭」
由 provincial 加 -ly 构成，义为「以地方的方式；带着地方气」

senses.title: A large administrative region of a country
senses.definition: a large area of a country with its own local government, smaller than the whole state
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家中设有本地政府的大区域，范围小于整个国家
senses.example: She was born in a farming province in the west.
senses.exampleCN: 她出生在西部一个以农业为主的省。
senses.why: Latin provincia first named a duty assigned to a Roman official and only later the territory attached to that duty, so the word begins as a job before it becomes a piece of land.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provincia 最初指分配给罗马官员的一项职责，后来才指随这项职责而来的地盘；所以这个词先是一份差事，然后才是一片土地。

senses.title: An area of activity that belongs to someone
senses.definition: a subject, duty or area of activity that is properly someone's concern
senses.definitionCN: 某种学科、职责或活动范围，正当地属于某人负责
senses.example: Deciding the budget is the province of the committee, not of one member.
senses.exampleCN: 决定预算属于委员会的职权，而不是某一位委员的事。
senses.why: If a province is the territory that comes with an office, then any field that comes with a role can be called a province, and the word shifts from land to responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 既然 province 是随官职而来的地盘，那么随某个身份而来的任何范围都可以叫 province，词义便从土地转到职责。

senses.title: The parts of a country outside the capital
senses.definition: the regions of a country away from the capital, often treated as less central or less sophisticated
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家中远离首都的地区，常被视为不那么中心或不够时髦
senses.example: After ten years in the capital, he moved back to the provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 在首都待了十年之后，他搬回了外省。
senses.why: A capital is a province too, but once it becomes the seat of power the rest of the map is named as a plural mass, and the phrase in the provinces quietly carries a judgement about the centre.
senses.whyCN: 首都本身也是一个省，可一旦它成为权力所在，地图上其余部分就被当成一个复数整体来称呼；in the provinces 这个说法里，悄悄带着以中心自居的评判。

intro.en: Province comes from a Latin word for a duty laid on an official; where that Latin word itself comes from is still debated, and it is not related to the verb provide.
intro.cn: province 来自一个表示「交给官员的职责」的拉丁语词；这个拉丁词本身的来源至今仍有争论，它与动词 provide 并无同源关系。

items.en: Provincia named a charge, an office or a command given to a Roman magistrate, and then the territory that came with it; its own origin is uncertain, and a common guess links it to pro- plus vincere, to win.
items.cn: provincia 指交给罗马官员的任务、职位或兵权，后来也指随之而来的辖区；它自身的来源不确定，一般认为可能与 pro- 加 vincere（战胜）有关。

items.en: Under the empire the word settled on the governed lands outside Italy, each with a governor sent from Rome.
items.cn: 在帝国时期，这个词固定指意大利之外受管辖的土地，每一块都派有从罗马出去的总督。

items.en: Old French province kept both the administrative and the territorial senses and passed them on to English.
items.cn: 古法语 province 同时保留行政与地域两层意思，并把它们传给英语。

items.en: Middle English province named a church district as well as a region of the realm, so the word was already used for several kinds of division.
items.cn: 中古英语的 province 既指教会辖区，也指王国中的区域，所以这个词早已用于好几种划分。

items.en: Modern English keeps the political sense, adds the figurative sense of a field of knowledge, and uses the plural for everything outside the capital.
items.cn: 现代英语保留政治义，增加「知识领域」的比喻义，并用复数指首都以外的一切地方。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on or close to the Latin word for a province; the near-meaning group holds words for regions and fields of activity.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「行省」一词上或与其形近的词；近义组收表示区域与活动范围的词。

entries.definition: Relating to a province, or narrow in outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 与省有关的，或指眼界狭隘的。

entries.definition: Interest in one's own province, or a narrow local outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 对本地事务的关注，或狭隘的地方观念。

entries.definition: In a way that relates to a province or shows a narrow outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 以与省相关的方式，或带着地方偏狭地。

entries.definition: Foresight or care, from Latin providere; the spelling is close but the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 远见与照管，来自拉丁语 providere；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: A large area of a country or of the world.
entries.definitionCN: 国家或世界中的一大片区域。

entries.definition: An area marked off for administrative purposes.
entries.definitionCN: 为行政目的划出的区域。

entries.definition: A field of knowledge or activity under someone's control.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人掌控下的知识或活动领域。

entries.definition: A kingdom, or a sphere of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 王国，或某个活动范围。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a duty given to an official and ends as a piece of the map, and its family keeps turning on what belongs to whom.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「交给官员的一份差事」开始，最后落在「地图上的一块」，同族词始终围绕「什么归谁管」。

normal.en: Provincia in Latin was a job given to an official, and the land came second, which is why the word can still mean a duty today.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 provincia 是交给官员的一项差事，土地是后来才附上的，所以这个词今天仍能表示职责。

normal.en: The word is not related to provide: one comes from provincia, the other from providere, and their only link is a shared opening syllable.
normal.cn: 这个词与 provide 无关：一个来自 provincia，一个来自 providere，两者唯一的联系只是开头音节相同。

normal.en: Provincial adds -ial to make the adjective, and it carries both the neutral sense of local and the unkind sense of narrow.
normal.cn: provincial 加 -ial 构成形容词，既中性地表示「地方的」，也带贬义地表示「眼界窄的」。

normal.en: The plural in the provinces turns a map into a judgement, since it is always said from the point of view of the capital.
normal.cn: the provinces 这个复数说法把地图变成了评判，因为它总是从首都的视角说出来的。

normal.en: A church province and a political province are both divisions under one authority, which is how a single Latin word came to cover both.
normal.cn: 教会省与政治省都是在同一权威之下的划分，一个拉丁词就这样同时覆盖了两者。

abstract.en: A province is a piece of the map drawn by someone in the centre, so the word always carries a viewpoint.
abstract.cn: 省是中心的人画在地图上的一个格子，所以这个词里始终带着一个视角。

abstract.en: Calling a field your province is a quiet claim that others should keep out of it.
abstract.cn: 把某个领域称作自己的 province，是在不动声色地要求别人不要插手。

abstract.en: Empires divide land into provinces and people divide knowledge the same way, which is why one word serves both.
abstract.cn: 帝国把土地分成行省，人也照样把知识分成领域，所以同一个词能管两件事。

examples.en: She was born in a farming province in the west.
examples.cn: 她出生在西部一个以农业为主的省。

examples.en: Deciding the budget is the province of the committee, not of one member.
examples.cn: 决定预算属于委员会的职权，而不是某一位委员的事。

examples.en: After ten years in the capital, he moved back to the provinces.
examples.cn: 在首都待了十年之后，他搬回了外省。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若文斯」——听着像「评文事」，地方上的文书杂事都归它管，一个省就是这样一个摊子。

root: 拉丁语 provincia（交给官员的职责及其辖区），自身来源不确定，一般认为或与 pro- 加 vincere（战胜）有关；经古法语 province 进入英语，与 provide、provision 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a division under one authority; the senses divide into the administrative region, the field that belongs to a role, and the whole country outside the capital.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「在同一权威之下划出的一块」；义项分成行政区、归属于某个身份的领域，以及首都以外的整个地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map cut by straight boundary lines into large blocks, each with its own name and its own office.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张地图被笔直的边界线切成几大块，每一块都有自己的名字和衙署。

branches.en: a boundary line drawn across a map
branches.cn: 地图上画出的一条边界线

branches.en: a governor arriving at a distant seat of office
branches.cn: 总督抵达远处的治所

branches.en: a committee claiming a subject as its own
branches.cn: 把某个议题划归自己的委员会

branches.en: a train leaving the capital for smaller towns
branches.cn: 驶离首都开往小城镇的火车

branches.en: a field marked off like a province on paper
branches.cn: 像纸上行省一样被划出来的领域

intro.en: A Latin noun of assigned duty and its adjective hold the word together, while English endings turn the same stem into an adjective, a noun of attitude and an adverb.
intro.cn: 表示「分派职责」的拉丁语名词及其形容词共同支撑这个词，英语词尾又把同一词干变成形容词、表示态度的名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin provincia, a charge or a governed territory, and the adjective provincialis, of a province, stand behind the English word and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 provincia（职责、辖地）与形容词 provincialis（省的）是英语这个词及其同族词的来源。

definition_zh: 灰；灰烬；白蜡树
definition_en: the grey powder left after something burns, or a tall tree with hard pale wood
core_image: 火熄之后，灶底剩下一层细白的灰
scene: 壁炉里的木柴烧了整夜，早上只剩下粉末。 The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
sceneCN: 这里 ash 是「灰烬」（第 1 个义项：燃烧后剩下的粉末）；句意是炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：覆着灰的；灰似的

senses.title: Powder left by fire
senses.definition: the soft grey remains of something that has burned
senses.definitionCN: 某物燃烧后留下的松软灰色残余
senses.example: The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。
senses.why: Old English asce named the burnt powder, and the word has kept that sense for a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 asce 指燃烧后的粉末，这个词一千年来都保留着这一义。

senses.title: A tall hardwood tree
senses.definition: a tree with pale strong wood and winged seeds
senses.definitionCN: 木质浅色坚硬、结翅果的高大树木
senses.example: An old ash stands at the corner of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 田地角上立着一棵老白蜡树。
senses.why: This is a different Old English word, aesc, which happened to fall together in spelling and sound.
senses.whyCN: 这其实是另一个古英语词 aesc，只是拼写与读音后来与「灰」合流了。

intro.en: Ash joins two Old English words that came to look alike.
intro.cn: ash 合并了两个原本不同、后来形貌相近的古英语词。

items.en: asce meant 'ash, burnt powder'.
items.cn: asce 意为「灰、燃烧后的粉末」。

items.en: aesc meant 'ash tree' and also named the rune for it.
items.cn: aesc 意为「白蜡树」，也指代表它的卢恩字母。

items.en: Both words settled into the spelling asshe.
items.cn: 两个词都归入拼写 asshe。

items.en: The modern spelling ash became standard.
items.cn: 现代拼写 ash 成为标准。

items.en: The tree sense survives mainly in wood and plant names.
items.cn: 树木义主要保留在木材与植物名称中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ash family; the near-meaning group gives other burnt remains.
note.cn: 形近组是 ash 词族；近义组是其他燃烧残余。

normal.en: The word is one short syllable: ASH.
normal.cn: 这个词只有一个短音节：ASH。
